You ever think about setting up that research trip in Ireland? I heard the visa rules are still pretty lax.      I might.

Right, I just wanted to bring up something I’ve been thinking about all week. Don’t get me wrong, I’m not trying to start an argument—but I feel like we need to talk about how we manage household responsibilities at the flat. I’ve been doing most of the cleaning, like every day, and it’s beginning to grind on me. I’m not asking for a 50-50 split, but I’ve noticed you’re less on the ball this month, and I’m a bit worn out.      Okay, first of all, thank you for bringing it up. I know I’ve been a bit out of it these past weeks. I’ve been working like a dog on that new project and haven’t had a great sleeping schedule. I’m not trying to take you for granted, honestly. I’m just a bit tired and I think I’ve been relying too much on you to pick up the slack. I appreciate it more than I probably say. What are you suggesting?      I’m not fussed about the exact details so much as just having a bit more help. I do notice you’ve taken the bins out more times recently, though, so points for that! But I think it’d help if we had some sort of schedule or system. Like a task rotation or something. I know it sounds boring, but I feel like it would take the pressure off me. And maybe you set up a reminder on your phone?      Yeah, I get what you mean. I’ve just been in one of those moods where my brain is already overloaded with work stuff, and I’m not very good at remembering the little admin stuff at home. That’s probably not fair on you. I can try to make a bit more time for it. And I can set up those reminders. Maybe a shared calendar app between us?      That sounds good. No pressure to step up overnight, but over the next few weeks, maybe you can help a bit more with cleaning, washing the dishes, and something like laundry once a week? I’ll even take the lead on making a shared to-do list.      That’s totally doable. I think it would help if I took the stress out of it and just did a bit more every day, instead of leaving it堆积 up on the weekends.

Rather annoying the wet weather, eh?      Aye, it's been damp as a cellar all week. Never had such a January for so long I can't remember.      I was out with the garden shear the other day—  Lottie  —Deirdre’s een beginning to forget things, don’t think they want   her   looking after the dachshund a week. A shame too; he's such a darling little chap.      Aye, it’s a rough spot for the carers when the parents start to get the  foggies , like. My old Elizabeth couldn’t even tell the difference between the teacup and the ashtray about a year before she went. Still, best to have someone in the house more or less full-time.      I think the world’s moving too fast for some of us old ‘uns. I see all those fancy tablets and touch-screen things... I used to build viaducts and plan culverts, not bloody   Google Maps  !      Oh, I do like the way the computer works out the maps for you though. Like a magic book. Did you know you can look up places from Norfolk and zoom in right down to where the little church used to be?      True enough, but I still take the Haynes Atlas every time I go somewhere. All that swiping and tapping’s too much for my poor fingers at this stage, and the old brain likes the certainty of a printed map.      Aye, certainty. That’s a luxury these days. Everything in the world’s being ‘streamlined’ and  updated  as they call it, about five times a year.      Humph! We were streamlined out of a house and a larder that was   updated   into housing estates long before any of that. My, time hasn’t exactly been kind to us!      Aye, well, it gives a chance to slow down and have a good long yarn about things. I was reading the other day—there's a bloke out in space trying to catch orbiting rocks by wrapping ‘em in nets the size of football pitches. Can you imagine trying to capture a space boulder with go-kart equipment?      That so? Sounds like a line out of a science fiction magazine. I’ve got one on the shelf from 1958. All rockets and tin men and girls with hair like curtains.      It’s a right laugh, isn’t it? When I was working at the creche I used to have my girls sit around for hours acting out the  Trip to the Moon , like.

So, I heard you've been working on your Honest Skincare business a bit more—the packaging came in first... What next on your to-do list?      Oh, thank you! Yeah, I've finally got the jars and the labels sorted—some were a bit wonky, but it's all good now. I'm testing out the 'before and after' photo thing on Instagram. Though I reckon I look a bit daft in some of the snaps, but hey, it gets views, right?      Definitely. You're doing all the right things with the socials. I like the branding—it feels very  you . I mean, the name, the colors, the vibe. So that’s honest, simple, natural—check, check, check.      You're sweet, thanks. I think honesty is key. I want people to trust the product, not just get dazzled by fancy packaging.      And that works, especially with eco-conscious buyers, you know? I had a student the other day who told me she only uses brands that are cruelty-free and zero plastic. Might I add, your products are both.      Exactly. I’ve been trying to keep the ingredients local where I can. I got the lavender from my nan’s garden, and I mixed in some rosehip oil from a woman down near Worcester. It’s not much, but every little helps.      That’s brilliant. People love that sort of story. Maybe you could add a little section to your website that explains the production—where each ingredient is from, how you make the products, that sort of thing.      I did think about that. I’ve started a blog area, but I keep procrastinating. I’ve got this vision of it being perfect, and I get bogged down in the details—like how to measure for the product dimensions for Amazon.      Oh, me too. I remember when I was sorting out the content guidelines for Japan, I had to research units versus metric measurements for weeks. I ended up listing both—millilitres and ounces. It was easier to do it once and let the system auto-convert for different countries.      Actually, I need to figure out the units for shipping too. I made a boo-boo when I sent a 50ml face serum to the US and it was measured in cm, not inches. The customer was confused about the size.      True, and sometimes it’s not just the dimensions but the weight and the content listing.

Rather annoying isn’t it, this weather.      Aye, it’s been like that all week. Never know whether to wear a coat or not! How are you feeling, love? Still not sleeping well?      Worse! I’ve taken to drinking warm milk again and all that’s done is make me need the loo half the night. I tell you, it’s enough to drive a person mad.      You know, I read in the paper last week that light therapy might help with the sleep issues. Something about getting out in the morning sun to reset the body clock. Still, I suppose that’s easier said than done, especially with how little light we’ve had.      Oh, left it a bit late to go on about the weather, didn’t you? I think I turned 66 last week, by the way.      You what? Well, bloody hell! I knew it was coming, but I never thought I’d miss it. You didn’t have a party, I hope—      Only with the cat, and I mean that seriously. What did you read in the paper about, by the way?      Oh, it was all about how staffing levels at the school are getting tighter. I’ve had to take on an extra class while the supply teacher is out. Again. Honestly, I’m not sure how much more I can give.      Well, I for one am glad you’re still giving it your all. Not many people out there anymore—especially not with the way money and politicians are running wild.      You said it. I remember back in the days you were the head of my class, you were always so strict but fair. Still are, I bet!      Maybe in my head, but I’m quite proud to say that I’m passed that now. Though I have been helping a few young teachers out on the side. Nothing intense, just helping them understand the kids these days.      That’s good to hear. Do they ever ask about the old days?      Oh, believe me, they do. I told one of them the other day how we used to walk uphill both ways to school in the snow just to learn our times tables. He looked at me like I’d lost my mind.      Ah, but he’s one of those digital kids now, never had to worry about a cold wind or a broken chalkboard.

So did you manage to sort out the central heating yet, Tom? I know it's been freezing in and out of the house lately.      I did, thank you! It was a dodgy thermostat. £200 later and it’s whirring like new. Although honestly, I'm thinking about just chucking the whole system and getting one of those heat pump things. You know, with that eco-bonus?      Oh, we had one of those installed a few years ago! It slashed our energy bill and doesn’t chase the temperature the same way a traditional heater does. It makes the house feel  much  more balanced, honestly.      That’s interesting. I still can’t get my head around the idea of not burning fossil fuels to keep warm. I suppose it makes sense long-term, financially and for the environment, but breaking the old habits is hard.      Well, here in Wales, we don’t usually need the heating! We just wear more layers and keep the fire going. That, or endure a few degrees and tell anyone who walks in that it’s the perfect ambient room temperature.      And welcome to my November. One of those days where the sky refuses to give light and the only heat source is the oven. Speaking of which, Rachel, how does your Christmas dinner thing work? You’re not hosting again, are you?      No, I’m not, but I might just bring the chicken and stuffing again. Last year my crispy shallots stole the show. I think someone made a shrine out of them in the kitchen.       Shrugs  I’ll bring about five different vegetables. My dad brought a man-getting-married list last year and a lasagne that had gone off. Not that I’m bitter.      Fair enough, but for the record, your guest list generates more drama than my work health and safety reviews.      Speaking of, I tried making mulberry jam this weekend. Weeds everywhere, but  somehow  edible.      Mulberries? At home? I thought the birds usually got to them before you did.      They go for the ripe ones—the unripe ones I get to trade in for jam. It’s a symbiotic relationship.      And your tools? How’s the sustainability angle working for you? I see you’ve got that tool off-lease scheme now, hearing from your Facebook rants about ‘buying tools when I’m not even sure I’ll use them.’

Rather annoying isn't it, this cutlery? It's tarnished again. Someone needs to polish it properly.      Oh, come on, Rach, it's silver plated, not proper silver. It's £20 a plate and we're moaning about it now?      Both of you, hush. You want your dinner to cool? Though I’ve been meaning to say — I think that this lot has been in the house since the 80s. My sister used to polish it every year when she lived in, what was it now? Mansfield, prior to moving out West. She'd line it all up and shine it to a mirror.      Yeah, I remember that. She left it in this box under the stairs once for weeks, and I thought it was old tools. When I finally opened it, I nearly dropped it all back when I saw it was cutlery. It was like in a museum crate, you know?      You lot and your fancy words. I reckon we’d all be better off chuckin’ it in and buyin’ some decent stuff — modern, unbreakable, and not worryin’ about tarnish. I’ve had enough of scraping rhythm and blues from the walls. Let’s upgrade?      Yeah, Dad, you’ve had enough of everything by now, haven’t you?      Our food’s not in the cutlery! That stuff was a gift from my brother-in-law when he made partner! He got a red carpet in the office, and this lot came with it in a box! He nearly did a backflip when he opened it. Standing in the hall, elbow deep in thimbles and forks! Not that I've ever worn it, but it's tradition. My grandma had the same set. She put her fork down once, and it sailed across the room like it had a life of its own.      Grandad, I don't know whether to laugh or cry. Auntie Websites mentioned once that the lunches back then were “hurried affairs” because everyone was worried about the cutlery.      Oh yes, that’s my parents’ story too. If a sauce got too acidic, they’d separate out the spoons. They were big on "proper service."      Honestly, it feels like this cutlery has its own union, right? You don’t just use it — you have to appease it somehow.      Now that I can get behind. Maybe we hold a symbolic “repolishing of old unions” night once a year.

Rather skip to the moon in the snow weekend, Christopher, do you recall saying that last time?      No, no, I’m more of a football kind of person      Right, but we do need the trip, children frightened      Right, but we do need the trip, children frightened      But I wanted to come with a snowball fight      Of course, love. Oh but skiing, though, pulling someone along. Christopher, how was your day?      Okay Mummy      Did you make anything new?      In school? No, boring like always My turkey came back with a C      Ten more, see if I can get them, push and I’ll get the little pigs to take them for you      What pigs?      Haha in the park next door, the oversized desktop hides, you remember them      Yeah, those were funny      We need to plan this up next weekend though, your uncle Paul is coming back early      Good, he takes us ice skating      So is that a –      Yeah, I know      Yeah, I don’t know if he can phone me if I’m already gone      He's going someone      Yeah, my friend Lyn is coming down oddly, I think she needs something      Like a baby sitter?      Haha not today about skiing, I think she's brought a man      Again?      Yeah, she's barely left the house, unwell      Should we put the chickens in guestrooms      Haha no, the chickens are going to Lichfield      So when do we get to the skiing?      Friday morning, we take lunches, keep the chocolate with your sandwiches      Do you get something for me skiing like a man      I think your man is gone      Again?      He’s a bloke on the trains your age      I am 3, mummy      I’ll take photos of both of us      Like when we went to the park      Yeah like that, but there will be snow      Mummy, can Uncle Paul take me for adventure park again      Maybe before skiing, we can have small mountain first      Yes, adventure park, that is fun with snow      But remember, our holiday is to ski, not just adventure. Would you mind?      No, if there is food like fried donuts      Check, Mummy will bring extra snacks. How does Saturday work for meeting your dad?      Yes           By the way, your homework, do you have it finished?           …I don't know how to do the drawing essay about my dream      Right love, just draw a snowy mountain and a pig in a ski suit.

So did you get the homework done for tomorrow? I couldn't be bothered starting it last night.      No, I haven't even opened my books! I stared at the clock for ages and thought, “I can do this in ten minutes,” but then  rip  it was past midnight and I couldn't face it.      Same! My mum actually caught me on the Xbox and said, “You're doing that after you've done your Spanish.” So she disconnected it!       laughs  Is that your new punishment, or what? You know I saw the Spanish teacher last week, and he was saying we need to start thinking about whether we do GCSE or not.      Yeah! I’m telling you, I’m half thinking I’ll just do it because I’ve been dragged through it for four years now, but the other part of me doesn’t want to waste time if I’m not going to use it at GCSE.      Exactly. I mean, I want to do it, but I was over at my aunt’s for dinner and she was asking about it and said, “You speak fluent French and Spanish? What’ll you do with that?”      Oh, don’t get her started! My nan’s been bugging me since I was ten to study languages. “You can work in the EU,” “You can be a translator.” She never shuts up!      Haha, but it’s also kind of handy knowing stuff like conjugations and grammar. I remember being in food tech and thinking, “How do I say ‘boil’ in Spanish when I’m explaining my recipe?” I just panicked.      Oh, yeah, I had to look it up online and write it down so I wouldn’t mess up. The problem is, in school, they say ‘Revise the lesson’ and then you have to actually remember that vocabulary at 6 a.m. on the bus.      I miss when we did just stick to basics, you know? Like in primary, we always used to do songs or act stuff out. Now it’s just translations and vocabulary lists and I’m like, “Who even speaks like that in real life?”      I think they should have made it like a language app, you know? The kind where you get points and your avatar does cool stuff. That would get people to actually learn it.      Totally! But anyway, what’s next after school for you?

Rather skip the new horror flick they're on at the cinema. I've had enough jumping out of my skin for one weekend. Never mind sitting through a whole film of it!      Aw, it's not that bad! I went to see it at the Odeon in Lewisham and it was more  atmospheric  than scary. I reckon it's more about the story than the jump scares.      Mmm, maybe. But since I watched   The Conjuring  , I haven't been the same. Still can't sleep when it's raining heavily. You'd think I was young enough to make it a laugh.      That's why I like watching them with you, Nan. It makes me feel like I’m doing something  good . I mean, what else is the point of being a good little horror fan if you can’t terrify your better half?      Well, you did drive me to a full week of jumping at shadows once, remember the ghost house scene in that one? I still don’t like walking through the hallway if the lights flicker.      Right! I’ve still got grief from that, by the way. My mother watching us during a call and thought you were actually being haunted. She sent me a book on exorcisms and how to stay safe in the home.      Ugh, don't even remind me. I don't know what's worse: being haunted by a ghost in a movie or being haunted by your own family's bad decisions.      Fair point. So, what  are  you watching instead? I heard you’ve been into those old romantic dramas from the eighties.      Oh yes, I'm a  massive  fan of that love triangle film with the telephone box.  On the Phonebox Edge , I think it was called.      You mean  When Harry Met Sally ? That was ‘89.      You're getting your films mixed up, dear. I meant the one with the telephone box and lunches on a Tuesday. More dramatic.      Oh,  The Dinner . Mm! The one where the guy's really on the fence about getting back together with his first love and his line is, “It was complicated,” in three different inflections depending on your mood.      Exactly! You see? We understand each other. Much better than we do with this new horror stuff.      Definitely. On the other hand, maybe the horror film wasn’t so bad if it gave us  two  entries on the CBBC movie casting call for “scared elderly person.”

Rather annoying isn't it, this weather.      That's it, it's like it's making up its mind whether it's going to be a summer at all or not.      Not to mention the fact I had to cancel my motorbike lesson two weeks in a row now and now I've got to start all over again.      Yeah, I saw that on your Facebook.      Oh right, you are on there, are you?      Yeah and when you're not, I keep an eye on you for the rest of the family mostly.      What, no you don't? You like spying on me, don't you?      Ten out of ten for the sarcasm. But I was sad not to see your photo with your new leathers on.      I know I've been wanting to ride for so long and my dad said ever since I was little, didn't he.      He did, yeah and he always thought it was inappropriate for a girl really I mean short skirt flapping in the wind and all that.      Oh come on, it's not like that.      Mate it's got a motocross leathers on it and huge gauntlets and visor and that's what you wear for a quad bike and that's not even the same class of machine.      But I still read books about it and watched videos and I got out with my uncle plenty of times in the countryside and being told I was safe all the time.      Yeah I mean your dad's brought you up right, you're not reckless. But I suppose he was just being old fashioned.      I suppose so but I do just wish I could do the lesson rather than sit in here mucking about on the internet with my students.      Oh come on, your students miss you madam. We had to tell them over the weekend to send you a text or a 'hey miss Granger message' or whatever it's going to be called these days.      They sent me go karts on pond life if you don't mind or at least made me feel better, I suppose.      You're what your dad used to call a pest sometimes.      Oh I'm a pest, am I? It's not like you complain about me coming over either.      I wouldn't have my daughter near me at all if I was completely honest.

Rather annoying isn't it, eh? You think when you do a PhD you’d get out of teaching first years, and then it turns out you’re doing more than ever!      I know, it’s mad. I’ve had to cancel my Thursday lecture twice now because it was booked for a meeting and there’s no space to rearrange. I feel like I'm living in the admin calendar.      Honestly, I’m just waiting for the day I turn into a spreadsheet. “Name: Lucy. Status: Overworked and underappreciated.”      Get in, jokes about yourself!  laughs  I just wish we could afford to hire another lecturer for the department. My postgrads are swamped.      I hear you – I had Oliver in again this morning. The poor lad is crying because he can't find a dataset for his thesis. I told him if he keeps pulling his hair out I’m going to start charging for sympathy.      You and your sense of humour. Speaking of which, I saw the shop by the station is open again—remember the one with the weird health products?      Oh, you mean the one where they sell lemon and turmeric everything like it’s the miracle cure for all of modern medicine? I bought their ‘detox smoothie mix’ once and swore I had carbonation in my sinuses for a week.      That’s the one. Well, they’re now also selling ‘adrenal energy bites’ and ‘keto-aligned glitter’ for some reason. I thought, if I want keto glitter I will patent it myself.      I mean, I’m not the same feminist I used to be, but glitter is glitter.  laughs  Speaking of, shall we pop in before the housing office does up the prices again? My cereal stash is running low and I need something high in sugar to survive the rest of the week.      Sounds like a plan. I need some tea leaves too. We ran out and I cannot teach without being able to sip something warm with lunches of sandwiches and biscuits.      Me too. Honestly, I miss cafes and proper meals sometimes. Don’t go getting any ideas about cooking Thai food or I’m walking straight out of this line.      Who, me? Don’t be ridiculous. I make toast at the level of culinary excellence.      And yet, I choose to stand by your side.      That’s love, my dear. That’s love.      Only when the love includes tea and emergency snacks.

Right, so the plan’s this weekend for us to go out. I was thinking Saturday afternoon? The kids can play and I’ll get some time to see my friends properly.      Mmm, is it? Not sure I like the word  babysitting . Make it  babysymbol-sitting !  Tickety-boo !      Yeah, let’s just say  babyming  this weekend. I’ve had friends asking for ages to get together, it’s just been tricky with the schedule and whatnot. But if Grandma and Grandpa can take the little ones Friday night, we can have a proper plan.      Grandpa can have me? My turkey leg?      Yes, Grandpa has plenty of turkey legs, and stories about tractors and cows. You’ll be  very  busy.      He doesn’t have cows. He told me last time he saw a cow and it was hides, Grandad’s property. Also, he once fell off a quad bike.      Ooooh, was he okay? Did he land on a toadstool?      No, it was quite a stumble. But he landed okay—he just shouted a lot at the quad, and now it won’t go up hills unless he sings to it.      Should I bake some cookies for Grandma? She said she’s going to read someone a story and nap on the sofa. I could draw her a card.      That’d be lovely. Or you can both be ‘tiny helpers’ in the kitchen. Maybe we make your famous about-‘accidentally-tasted-the-raw-butter’ cups this time.      No! Those were not  mine . I was just near the spoon.      Oh yeah, you  were  near the spoon. Parents were  not  happy. I remember you said ‘It smelled like clouds fell in a cave!’      Right. Anyway, if we’re doing this weekend, we need to plan what to do with the kids. Maybe Friday night after dinner, they can head over and the four of us go out Saturday?      Can we go to the park? Is it pirate day again?      Well, depending what your Grandma and Grandad are up for. Maybe pirate day, maybe library day, maybe tea with the cat people.      Can we have a camera this time when we go to the park? I want to take selfies with the ducks and post it on  My Little Wall of Beautiful Things .      Only if you promise to also take a proper photo of Grandad before he goes, while he still remembers where he left them.      Oh, he left his glasses on the space rocket.

Okay, I swear this sandwich is 90 per cent mayonnaise and 10 per cent  what used to be chicken . Have you tried today’s lunch option?      Oh, I went for the “vegetable stir-fry” and let me tell you—it looked more like it had been cryogenically frozen and then told to take a nap for 12 hours. Honestly, I’ve had better from my nan’s microwave in the 80s.      Haha, same! This canteen makes me miss my nan literally, but also  nothing  else. I went out last night, tried this new spot near town—Harmony, it’s called? It’s that one with the neon sunset wall and the chill DJ playing Lana Del Rey. You should’ve seen the Darcy Lewis lookalike in there. I nearly had a nosebleed.      Ooh, that place? My cousin went there for her 21, said the oversized loaded nachos were the main event. Also, the guy who brought her was so posh he called the limes “citrus segments” IRL. It’s a student spot, but it only pretends to be.      GIRL. I will do  anything  for those nachos. Should we ask the others to come with us tomorrow? We’ve been studying like hermit crabs since Term started and I haven’t left this library sector since the hills were alive with the sound of someone not booking a study room in advance.      Yeah, let’s do it. Though, is it just me or does uni feel like this alternate universe where  time is broken ? I dropped about five lectures last week because I kept tripping over the fact that I had no idea what day it was.      I felt the same. I was like, “Is this a time loop or just burnout?” Honestly, I miss sixth form. I miss the way the canteen was just greasy chips and relish, you know? Like, at least the chips had  flavor .      Oh please, I miss the English teacher who made us write 500-word essays on “The Significance of the Duck” because gothic literature had pond life vibes. Not everyone got it at first.      I  still  don’t get it. But what can I say, we all have our fluency in nonsense. Although, I did go to this lecture by someone from the university press last week and they basically sound like they’re speaking Latin and I was like…  this is my third week here, and they’ve already lost me .

So did you lot actually manage to get anything to eat in Cambridge or did you just get takeout again like everyone else?      Nah, we actually popped into this little Indian place by the library. I don’t think we’ve been there before. It was called  Harmony Haber . Got a bit of a wait, but the biryani was mad good.      Oh yeah, that place? My flatmate went in too last week. She said it was alright, but not as spicy as the one in Leeds she used to go to. Apparently, the chicken korma there is like, literally dipped in Laksa leaf and something else.      That sounds mad. I’m more of a simple kinda gal — you know, cheese on toast and a fried egg if I’m feeling fancy, which I’m not. Honestly, I had takeout again — just Chicken Tikka Masala, no questions asked.      I’m starting to think the whole takeaway is an excuse not to cook anymore. Like, I used to actually cook real food—stews and things—but now it’s like, five takes on falafel and a banana bread recipe from grief support.      Oh please, banoffee pie? That’s a staple. You’re trending at the top of the Royal Society of Baking, aren’t you? Honestly, the only thing better than takeout is holidays. Silly question, but who’s going anywhere nice for August?      Oh no, I’m not. I just thought about it and I can already feel the flinch—sunset over the hotel pool and being like,  do I  actually  want to do this again? . I’m staying local. Maybe head to Whitby or something. It’s like a two-hour drive, right?      Whitby is a classic. I went there with my mates for like four years in a row after A-levels. The fish and chips there were mental. And the beach was  freezing , but there’s something about the pier at night. Feels like  Crimson Peak  or whatever.      A bit Gothic for me, but I get it. I prefer something a bit tamer—camping by the go lakes or something. My partner wanted to go to Tenerife, obviously. I was like, “We could go further and stay in a hostel and get a better tan at half the cost.” Eventually we settled on a cabin in the Scottish Highlands.      Oh right? So like, full adventurers now? Only I’m surprised they went for that—close enough to signal to hike and get lost?

Rather skip the newfit and go to London to see me. A few people in our youth hostel in Cornwall have got to go, including me. Otherwise I shall find I can't cover the expenses.      Oh, we wouldn’t have wanted you to miss out, dear. It was nice of you to invite us, though we were a bit worried about the budget. My George wanted to come, but with that car breaking down every other week...      Oh, don’t get me started on that. We’ve been meaning to replace it for ages. Apparently, the kids say you can get a good deal on eBay if you know what you're doing, but the idea of sorting through shipping and warranty like that—yikes.      Yeah, we tried that once, didn’t work out too good, the one I bought turned up with a flat tyre and a seat missing.      Well, if you ever want some tips, I used to run a childminder service and we used eBay to get spare bits for the mini bus. Worked well—just took patience.      That’s the problem I suppose, patience. I’ve still got grief from teaching, where today’s problem is solved by 3 p.m., and then tomorrow gives you a whole new headache.      Right enough, it's all good until you hit a new set of tests and evaluations again. Silly if you ask me, don’t seem to teach the kids much just sharpen their pencils and get them ready for a government tick box.      Oh, you had the letters going on in London as well. The election stuff—I don’t know what it’s come to, about half the people I know don’t even know what the different parties do.      Same here. The last lot of new government rules have me unimpressed. I do miss a time when local councils could make decisions for themselves.      Aye, the more they introduce, the less it makes sense. Still, I suppose when I sort out selling the house in Norfolk and maybe shift to Harrow for a bit with your lot, I can enjoy the chaos from the sidelines.      You come with us dear! The house is still goin' on the market if you'd like to go over together and look about.      And I’ve got an estate agent near your place who’s supposed to have a few ranch-style houses—better for older folk.

So did you go and pick out a name yet? I mean, I know it's still early, but... you and Claire were talking about it the other day at my birthday dinner, remember?      Honestly? Not yet. I keep meaning to, but I get overwhelmed just thinking about it. I saw a list online the other day with 30 pages of possible names and all of them sounded like they were taken from a medieval saga or something! I just want something simple but meaningful, you know?      Oh, I get that. Didn’t your mum always say she wanted to name you Eleanor but your dad liked Mary better because "Eleanor sounded too posh”? That always made me laugh.      Oh my God—you remember that? It’s ridiculous! I’m terrified I’m gonna name the baby and then in ten years someone’s going to point out that the name is better for a boy or whatever. I just want everyone to feel comfortable with it at the end of the day.      Honestly, the most important thing is that  you  like it and that you and Claire both feel good about it. I named my daughter Lila because her middle name is Hana and I thought Lila Hana had such a nice rhythm to it. Plus, it meant “a lot of light” in Arabic, and I kind of thought she’d be the light of our lives—turns out she’s more of the “messy toddler at the weekend café” kind of light. But still...      Oh man, I’ve already been to a café with you and her at half ten in the morning and it’s intense! I mean, your ballet slippers and your Apple juice with a straw—she does everything standing up! She’s adorable though. Honestly, I’ve already found myself staring at her when you’re out and thinking, “That’s my sister’s daughter, and that little girl is perfect.”      Aww, thanks. I know it sounds a bit dramatic, but once you have a baby you just... you sort of see the world differently, like every cute thing becomes a symbol of life and joy and all that stuff you used to brush off when you were 19 and thought having kids was just a hassle.      I know what you mean. I used to be all "no kids for me," and now I can’t believe I ever said that.

Morning everyone! Coffee or tea? I’ve just made a fresh pot.      Morning, love. I’ll take a tea, please, and I assume you haven’t skipped breakfast this morning?      No, I didn’t! I made some French toast for the lot of us and there’s jam and fruit on the table. I reckon it’s about time we all chilled a bit and stopped rushing so much.      Honestly, you’re right. I’ve barely sat down since we got in from the shops yesterday. Do you want me to pour you some tea, Dad?      Aye, love, and I appreciate the help. That toast smells well good, by the way. I swear it’s better when you make it, Janey. You’ve got the touch.      Blimey, thank you. I better not get too full of myself though, else Brian here will challenge me to a pan’s best ever toast!      Oh, I’ll tell you, your toast is leagues better than any café round here, Janey. Don’t let them puts you off.      That’ll do, Liza. You reckon you’re any good in the kitchen? You still taking the knife and fork with you just in case?      Oh, hush. It’s not funny. Anyway, I was meant to start that online course today for nursing and I’m just panicking in case I forgot the password.      I can help you with that. Also, have you seen the news this morning? They’re talking about more flooding in the west country. I about blocked out for an hour trying to write the copy for that charity this morning. It’s wild how much climate stuff is hitting the headlines now.      It’s not just news, it’s the reality. I was out at the practice yesterday and one of the ladies there said her mum was evacuated. Sounds terrible. I hope they’re alright.      Ugh, that’s awful. It’s always the countryside that gets a rough deal with these things. Speaking of, I’ve set the timer for the mower and I’m going to get the go ahead from the pond fish if they don’t mind me moving the header. Thought I’d do a bit of weeding while I’m at it.      That’s the spirit, love. You’ve been putting that off so long I was half expecting a toad farm in there by now.

So did you get your science results back yet? I’ve been dreading it all week.      Yeah, I did. I’m so annoyed I lost a few marks on the plant cells diagram. I swear I shaded in the chloroplasts properly!      Me too! My friend at Newton College said the test was ridiculous. I reckon it was harder than last year’s.      Honestly, that teacher’s got it in for us. Imagine setting questions about mitosis and photosynthesis in the same paper. Ugh. But, hey, at least maths was a bit easier this time.      Don’t remind me of the algebra. I managed to get the turkey one right, though — you know the one where you had to work out the cost of the ingredients and the rest of the recipe?      Oh yeah, that one. I still can’t figure out how half the class got the wrong answer. Maybe we’re all just not cut out for ordering percentages or something.      It’s not fair, really, when we have art class next and I can draw a whole scene in like ten minutes and only get a B. Whereas in science…      Well, from what I hear, Mr. Baptiste is super strict about the marking, but Miss Haywood is much more chill. Have you thought about doing textiles for your GCSEs?      Maybe. I want to work with plants one day anyway. My grandma has this garden in Linton that looks like an out-of-a-christmas-card fantasy land. She’s got these bluebells and snowdrops and there’s a gnome about five foot tall hiding behind the hydrangeas. She’s had it for years.      Oh that sounds amazing! I really like how she uses stamps in her flowerbeds. She made me one for my birthday last year — a sundial with all my friends’ names carved into it. Do you collect stamps? My nan collects them and I sort of stick to it too.      No, I've never really been into it, but the idea of saving a piece of history is kind of cool. Plus, if you get the right ones, you can make money from them or something.      I don’t really care about the money, I just like looking at the designs. The latest ones have that fluency to them, like they almost tell a story with the shapes and the symbols. But I did talk to my nan over the holidays, and she said she's growing a new plant this year that looks like a tiny tree.

Rather annoying this new bus route they've introduced, isn't it, Ethel? Me hop ‘n’ skip all the way from Costessey now because the 7X runs less often than a bad penny these days.      Oh, George, you must get your eyes tested again. They improved the service at Newton Park last spring, if I recall correctly. You just need to get up earlier. A gelatine breakfast and a walk in the garden, and you’ll be on it by ten.      Eyes are fine, and what’s the point if the bus takes ’em to a dead end near the filling station? I’ve no need to go to the pub only to find the closest stop is Myddelton Green, for goodness’ sake. It’s ridiculous! I’m old, not Oliver Cromwell, and I’ll be the first to say it.      Now, George, no need to get animated. I’m sure the council’s looking into it. We can always arrange a lift to the surgery or the shops. One of the young blokes from the bakery shop, Jake—?      Aye, quite a gem he is. Polite and always offers a slice of scone on the house. But don’t encourage him, Harry. He’s already doing enough with his shift at the garage, let alone ferrying old fogeys about.      Well, if he’s willing, we don’t say no, do we? Ethel, have you noticed the bus conductor’s changed to a smiling young chap with a tablet? Some folks still get confused about how the payment works. I’m not sure if it’s cheaper in the long run or not, mind you.      Paid touch here, tapped card there—juggling like a rat puppet at a fairground. I’d sooner handle cash. At least I know the smell of a real fiver between my fingers. All this blinking technology gives me the willies.      Oh, I love my tablet, George. It came with a birthday card from my grandniece. You can read out the vaccine schedule with it, keep the whiz kids in touch, and play Bingo online for tuppence a pop.      George, you really need to see about getting a new pair of glasses, though. You’d appreciate the design if you could see the blooming screen.      So I’m supposed to squint all day and hope it lands in the right slot?      Now, talk of slot—a few weeks back, I was at the church fete

So do you know what’s on near here today, Nana? I was thinkin’ ‘bout wanderin’ round a bit after this.      Well, I think there’s a little food market just up the road. They do proper continental bread and fresh olives. I’ve seen eeny every now and then.      Ay, that sounds good. I’ve a bit of a hankerin’ for some of that ol’ Italian bread. The kind that doesn’t crumble under a cup of coffee like the shops back home sell.      Oh aye, this place is mostly proper when it comes t’ food. I rememb’r when we first came here visitin’ Gran years ago. It used t’ be just a little fishy backwater, them canals and all. A world away from the telly, you know?      Bucksy? I mean, I’ve seen pictures, but it’s different now, innit? They even showed it on the news the other day, all dressed up for one o’ them festivals.      Aye, well it’s still got its charm. You can’t dismiss that. Real local shops, the old ones where the same people have been runnin’ for years. Not like the high street in Bolton these days—chain after chain.      Ugh, yeah. I miss the little shops. Smells like heaven in here, this café though. That smell of coffee and cinnamon…      Oh definitely. Some o’ the buns here, though—cakey, sticky stuff. Far more exciting than a plain croissant. I daresay your gran would’ve picked the most buttery one on the plate.      Definitely. She used t’ say it was a ‘posh crime’ just eatin’ one of them things. But if she had a fiver and a choice, she’d pick a cake over fish and chips any day.      Aye. She had her priorities. Look, if you’re game, after that market I could take you to the old bookshop. That one where they still got the smell of aged paper and the cat that go in and out?      You mean the one with the shelves almost touchin’ the ceilin’? Ay, I’ve seen it. It looked summat outta a film. Thought it was boarded up last time I was here.      Nah, still open, love. They’ve got them proper old books and the owner’s been there for near thirty years. Lovely cove. They even do readings on a Thursday sometimes.      That’s ace. So, market, then a book hunt, and then I reckon some fresh macarons for last stop?

So did I! The gym was absolutely packed last week, I swear they had to rope off the treadmill section!      Oh I saw that! I turned up on a Monday and nearly cried. I was like “ugh, I came for peace and low-intensity spin class, not a rush-hour tube at King’s Cross!”      I know! But I actually ended up joining a Zumba session instead by accident because the instructors were all changed, and honestly? I was sweating by the third verse. Who knew grinding was so athletic?      Oh God, I can’t dance like that without injuring myself! I made sure I stuck to the spin class, only to find out the instructor had My Chemical Romance playing for the warm-up! I’m a health marketing exec, not a Post-Grunge tribute act!      That’s an added bonus, don’t you think? I mean, whatever gets you to push through, right? Anyway, how are things at BUPA? Still working on that new campaign about holidays and heart health?      Ugh, yes! Our latest brief is basically written in emojis — “☀️ + 🍷 = 🚑” — but in good news, I’m working on a partnership with a local holiday booking site – trying to get “resort recovery” tips into the headlines instead of “how to survive airport security after three bottles of wine.” You know what it’s like.      Honestly, just someone telling people not to die from overhydration is already a win in my books. I’m working on something very niche at my end too – a project for repurposing office buildings into co-working gyms. Essentially, we’re asking “what if your Fitbit had a coffee machine?” It’s… a vibe.      Oh you’re telling me it’s a vibe? I bet the funding board had to put someone on “expected ROI in guinea pig form.” But hey, if the future is working out while you microwave your lunch, I’m here for it.      100%. Now, speaking of future plans, are you going on holiday with your parents again? I still can’t get over that time they caught you arguing with the ferry operator in gothic script on your holiday to Jersey.      Oh my God, don’t remind me. He didn’t know what a “bat” emoji was, and I was like  this is why we can’t have nice things . No, I’m not going this year – I made plans with a few friends to do a Europe road trip.

Rather annoying isn't it, this business with the bollards. I was just trying to get in and had to reverse twice, nearly gave the poor maintenance man a heart attack.      Oh heavens yes, and to think they claim it’s for safety. Just like the landlord’s idea of “improvements.” I swear if one more letter goes unanswered he’s just going to have to clean out with a brush and dustpan himself. Such a disgrace, honestly.      You’re right. We’ve had three different managing agents this year alone. It’s like they think the tenants are just to be juggle balls.      What’s worse is that people don’t even know what’s going on. I met an eccentric couple from France this morning – they live in the Champs-Élysées I think he said – came to see the Open Day at the exhibition. They’re fascinated by old British things, especially cathedrals. Though they were horrified about the Chichester Cathedral spire collapse.      Yes, that was a tragedy. Beautiful spire, too.      Oh quite! I’ve read quite a bit about its history. You know, they rebuilt it during the reign of Philip of Spain. Though I’m not convinced about the ones with the Romans, mind you – Mary Tudor certainly had the grit, though.      You’ve been to the archives in Spain? What was that like?      Oh yes! That was years ago, just before I retired. Mary’s letters were all there, handwritten in the original and still sealed in wax – all terribly exciting. You know, most people don’t even know what a real Tudor document looks like.      I can imagine! You know that reminds me of the book you were telling me about, the one on the Austrian battleship disaster. Have you sent anything to the British Library yet?      Soon, soon. I had to weave in some stuff about the bureaucrats there. We had to clear customs and that took as long as the war itself.      Ah the French! I’ve heard they’re particular, even around property and enterprise. The ones I met go every year on pilgrimage to Stratford. They think William Shakespeare is some Frenchman in disguise.      Oh the arrogance of the French! But you know, I’ve made it to every conference on European architectural history where those so-called anarchists had their day. Porden, the architect, he was quite the figure – and he wrote about that spire I told you of.

So did you lot actually do your homework for maths or are we doomed again?      I got it sorted, I copied it off Tom from year ten, he's like a maths genius or something.      That's not even us. Tom like,  dies  during IT lessons. You can't copy off him!      Classic. You're a doomed generation. Both of you.      No, no, she was joking! Look, if one of you was decent at English, me and Jack could get the coursework under control. I like to think of it as  group effort .      Ugh, GCSE English is the worst. I wrote my essay about my cat’s accident. Ten out of ten from my teacher, shouted, “Blimey, this is moving!” It was  terrible , but it worked.      Fair. My teacher said I sound like a robot. She thinks I'm writing in binary.      That’s because you do. I swear, you get sent to uni and start programming people.      Haha, only if they fail. Listen, have you guys seen the new comic issue of Beano? It's bonkers – Matey faces a challenge against a school-based AI that’s trying to replace the head teacher. It’s genius.      Oi, don’t talk about homework and then distract us with  comics . Honestly.      Wait, is it the one with the talking frog who steals crisps and then has a moral dilemma?      Ooh, I did  not  know about the moral dilemma part. That’s high quality. I read it on my phone at lunch. Proper laughs.      Honestly, I'd rather be reading that over reading the lesson plan that’s basically passed out by the bin.      Let's talk about  parents  for a sec. My little sister started junior school this year and my  mum’s  out every week trying to catch the teachers on camera with chocolate in their pockets or something.      My dad just phones the school every time I’m late. Even if I was seven minutes late walking over because I had to pick up a snack. He goes in with this face like “Is your son irresponsible?”      My mum and dad take it in turns. One week my dad dresses as a lawyer dad, the next, my mum’s walking in like, "He's 14, so he should be paying for his own snacks and his own school fees!"      That’s wild. My dad’s the kind who’s like, “Do your work.

Right, thanks a million for helping us sort out the clearing out. I know it's not exactly your first choice of weekend fun, Jonny.      Erm, nah, but I like doing it. Not all of it, but like, the bits with the books and stuff. Got eeny weeny bit of tech to trawl through too.      Oh, aye. A lot of this would’ve been from my university days. Poetry books, records... some interesting posters.      I might be able to reuse some of the branding ideas from the old shop signs. Maybe even make a bit of a feature of the branding out the front when we’re moving into that new place.      Yeah, we could do more with the space now the kids are all grown and gone. A bit of retail flair never did us any harm.      I was thinking this could be like a micro-market, kind of, you know, homeware, second-hand books, and maybe even small prints or photographs from the family’s history.      Oh, I love that! We could make it like a weekend event. Maybe start with a book swap on a Saturday, then a local food stall, and some music from Jonny – if he’s any good!      Erm, I’m not saying I’m brilliant, but I have played a few gigs already!      Now you’ve gone and put an idea in their heads. You know, I’ve thought about doing a talk on the Kendal High Street over the decades. Maybe even bring in a bit about education reform in the 1970s.      Oh, the good old days. Not much tech then, and not much retail that wasn’t a corner shop!      That’s true. And speaking of tech, Jonny’s already drawn up some ideas for the new website. Thought we could use a nice QR code system for the pricing – eco-friendly and modern.      Yeah, I’ve seen loads of places do that. I think it works!      Defo. But I think we need to think about the branding as go-to rather than just DIY. Something friendly, but still professional.      I suppose we could go with something modest – “Old Road Markets” maybe. It’s got character and feels local.      “Old Road Markets” sounds better to me than anything I could think of! Might give it a bit more history.      I like the sound of that. Reminds me of old Kendal, anyway.      To be honest, I think it needs some sort of plan.

So did you pick your GCSE options yet? I’ve been stressing about it for weeks.      I did last week. I’m doing art, music, triple science, and drama. What about you?      I’ve got music, like you, but then history and geography and single science. I’m still twitching about not doing drama. I wanted to do it but my mum said it wasn’t serious enough. Honestly, I don’t see why not. It’s not like it’s easier than history anyway.      Honestly, I told my dad I’d like to go into sound engineering or maybe be a music therapist when I’m older. He was like, “You’ll need a proper education first.” So I got extra English and maths. I’m not obsessed with GCSEs, but I think it helps for uni if you want to do a creative course.      I dunno. I’m into YouTube influencers and stuff, you know, people like Casey Ho or Blossom. I mean, not like full-time, but I’d like to see if being a creator can be a job properly.      Oh yeah, Blossom’s amazing. She went from watching other people to making her own games. I wish I was good at that. I got fairly good at TikTok because I do dance, but the views are basic.      You should make some stuff about school! Like, homework hacks or how to get out of PE. Honestly, I’d die to watch that. PE is so unnecessary. Some people just don’t have a sporty bone and being made to run laps all week is bullying, in my opinion.      I used to play clarinet in the orchestra but I gave it up last year. It was so tiring and I didn’t get a lot of attention for it. But I still like music. My sister’s in a YouTube band with her mates—they do covers and it’s going viral a bit.      That’s mad! My brother watches their videos and he goes on about how they’re always trying to sound like Ed Sheeran or someone. I asked him who that was and he said I had to be joking.      I think he means Liam or something.      Whatever, I’m not into any of that bloke stuff. I’d rather listen to queer artists or female rappers. I think girls are doing more amazing stuff now, like Billie Eilish or Inhaler.

Rather annoying this new tablet of mine. You know, me being old sticks and all, it’s not like I got the hang of tablets when they were first introduced. I can take photos, I can watch a little telly… but no, they have to fanny about with software now. It was working fine een time and now  this . Kept twitching and saying “update” every five seconds.      Aye, I know that! I got me one of them big chunky phones, you know the one you chuck in the river and it still works when it don't float. Had to fetch the grandkids in from school  this  mornin’ and it kept going off like some kind of posh turkey. “Updating security features” it said. Well, IToUpdate or toOpen the school gates?      Awww, leave it be dear, they’ve got to make something a bit more complicated these days than just switchin’ on and pointin’. I remember the day desktops used to have “32k of RAM” and we were walking around thinking we were millionaires.      Yeah I mean, don’t get me started. Modern tech is moving  so  fast there’s no possibility for people to catch up. When I got home from work yesterday – lecture on AI ethics, I might add – I tried to show my mum the weather app on my phone and she kept asking me why I didn’t just mail the postman for the forecast.      That’s right. And not to mention the cars these days. I was out with my son the other day and his car started talkin’ at him –  talkin’ , mind you. “Heads-up,” it says. “Turn the corner now.” I says to him, "Son, this vehicle gone gone loose in the head."      That's right. My nephew ‘ad one of them electric ones. All quiet as a mouse. I thought me grandkids threw a shindig in it. No growlin’ engine, no backfiring – just  click click  and off it goes. No brass bumpers 'n' no character whatevers happened to the good old RAC man delivering a car with three wheels and the rest made of go-kart?      If it ain’t respect for the past in the present, I don’t know what is. You know what your lot forget? The joy of visiting The Broads on a Saturday, where you see those beautiful herons and bitterns, right? I saw a ‘bittern’s nest at the end of last summer near Mangapps Water.

Rather skip the school uniform entirely. I remember one lad in our village who wore just his dad’s old pinstripe suit and polished Doc Martens every week. Blows their minds, it does. Now there was a lad with £20 spread over £200 worth of things gone wrong.      Oh, I used to trawl the charity shops for bits and bobs. You know, you could get a proper little suit done in a day, if you knew where to go. I once found a cardigan with a moose embroidered on the back for a child whose image of a “classy animal” was a bit . . . woolly. The poor thing didn’t know what to make of it. Want to go to  Marks and Spencer  today? They opened a new one near us.      You want to go for lunch or for shopping?
