So did you watch The Undateables last night? I mean, I know it's cringe, but honestly, the episodes are often so laugh-out-loud good I can't even handle it.      Oh yeah! That one bloke—what was his name again? The one who waited two and a half hours to leave his flat 'cos he was “unshaven” and “his clean socks were in the laundry”.      Timmy? Yeah,   that’s   the one! And the girl who said she doesn’t chase boys, but the bloke looks like a frozen cow and she still laughs at everything he says. Honestly, the people are only there for the cameras now. My nan still thinks it’s all real though. She says, “I know the real date goes better than the pickles they make on the show.”      Cats would definitely do better, no doubt. I just happened to watch a doc on Eastern European board games last night as a weird way of indulging my post-university ennui.      Oh, you’ve had some of those—right? I remember we tried a Polish game once. I think it was called “War on Borders”?      Yeah, that one! It was so pretentious it made me fairly proud of my Monopoly addiction. But anyway, the film said some of those games were like centuries old. One involved building villages and trading spices via ox caravans. They had rules in four languages and two boards: one for the peasants and one for the lords.        Of course   they did. I still don’t get your colleague, Laura, trying to do an interview with someone who claimed they “had such bad posture watching films on DVD they lost all mobility.” That’s her direct quote. I mean, it   was   on The Undateables, so maybe it was embellished.      A bit, maybe. But it did make for great viewing. Oh, I tried that new spa place near me. We did one of those full-day deals—body scrub, massage, and lunches with people you’ve never met. It took an hour just to find the parking attendant.      Oh no go on then I didn’t know you were there.      Finally, someone sane to talk to in a spa full of people who were all trying to be someone else for the afternoon. I swear half the women had come pretending to be celebrities.      Same with that “spa weekend” we had at my brother's place.

Rather annoying this new washing machine eh?      Aye, it's like it's learning to dance and I'm not telling it the steps yet. I swear it's programmed to vibrate the whole flat at half eleven every night.      I wouldn't be surprised if it sent eeny weeny passive-aggressive texts as well.   "Dear User: I’ve been overfilled. I’ve taken notes. – DM."        Oh aye, and it’s like it’s one of them fancy ones where you have to chase it halfway round the internet to work out what the three flashing lights even  mean . "Error Code: 42, Philosophical Crisis Detected."      I’m living with you though. I’m not just replacing it because I like you, even if this thing is trying to murder me. Or at least, my duvets.      Fair 'nuff. Although... I  did  sort of chuck the manual in the fag ash bin near the back door. One time, when I fancied being clever.      Oh, really? Brilliant decision, Mr. PhD. So what are we having for dinner today then? Otherwise I’m just going to have to blame the washing machine and eat cereal at 8 pm.      Let's slap some chicken in the oven and chuck some of those new veg boxes you always get on the side. You know the mexican chilli kind from Ethical Sources in Porters Arms. They taste like they've been to a yoga retreat or something.      Aye, delicious and pretentious. That lot’s  definitely  going in the bin about five minutes after I open the packet. But it still makes me feel like I'm cooking for Greta Thunberg.      Well if she pops in, I’ll be sure to serve her baked beans in a bamboo fork. Keep it eco.      Oh, and any plans for the weekend? I tried watching that new Bond film on the telly Saturday and halfway through I just panicked. It was like trying to read a thesis on dystopian geopolitics with a heartbeat soundtrack.      I caught bits of it the other night. There's a scene where he drives a car that doesn't have buttons—just a robotic voice that says “Location locked; mission activated.” It’s what your washing machine’s been dreaming of becoming.      Yeah, I'm thinking maybe just a weekend of  relaxing —like, proper relaxing. You know, silence, a bag of crisps, and whatever Netflix is recommending to me today.

Rather annoying this VW thing isn't it? I suppose anyone with a car was affected in some way. We had a friend in Dublin who had to return his car after months of waiting for a fixed part.      Yeah, I read about it in the news. People were furious. I wonder how many of the ones affected were from the north. It seems like problems like this are always brushed over if you're not in London.      I don’t know about that, but what I  do  know is that car was the size of a dragon. I worked in the oil industry up north for a while, and even back then, everyone was talking about the transition to electric cars. You can’t put that off forever, you know.      Well, back in Dublin, the city was already pushing for cleaner air. If only the government up here did the same. Look at the housing costs down south—people are paying millions for tiny apartments, but in places like this, you can get a decent house for half the price. Still, the infrastructure isn’t built for it.      That’s true. My cousin moved to Manchester from Cornwall a few years ago. She said she got double the space for half the price, but it’s such a commute from here. I’m thinking of moving down myself, just not sure I want to pay what London asks.      London? Don’t even get me started. I could foresee a situation where the only people living in the North are people like us—retired or working from home. The younger generation can’t buy out here anymore.      I thought being older I’d have more house to myself, but no. I about considered getting a caravan for the summer just to clear the clutter. You’d be surprised how much you own when you are suddenly not working and have time to accumulate things.      That’s for sure. I’ve guest-edited transcripts for people who’ve just bought their first homes. They told me how stressful it was with mortgage rates and house prices waiting to drop. We’re not hearing as much about rural areas though. I always wonder if people move up and can't settle in.      That’s a risk. You can get a place up here for go-on £150k and have a proper garden.

Rather annoying isn't it, eh? You think they'd learn by now.      Learn what, dear?      Going off at people! You say one thing, and next thing it's full-blown row. Look at George—just 'cause I mentioned moving the garden fence eeny bit.      You didn't explain he might think it all needs uprooting.      Fair dos, but I don't want to upset people. Yet it’s like trying to talk to brick wall sometimes.      That's the bloomin' modern world for you. No patience! In our day, you’d sit and talk, drink a cuppa and sort things.      I still do. I run out of patience, mind you, but I still try.      Ah! Blimey, speaking of patience—have you looked at your pension yet? I mean, with all the figures and numbers and ticky boxes.      Aye. I got the form through, sat down—thought I’d tell you—personally I can’t see half of it. Like a different language altogether. I only did A-level maths, but this… this is engineering, innit!      Let me see. I might have a younger neighbour who's good with these things. Can pop over sommat.      Good idea. Bit cheeky, but at our age, what the 'ell?      Just trying to stay afloat, love. Not a penny to rub together, is it.      I know. I had to come off the B&B in Bury St Edmunds—used to be the best place. Quiet, friendly vibes. But no more budget! Going stir-crazy at home.      Maybe we could do something, like a little group. Just get out once in a while. A bit of fresh air, a slap-up meal.      That’d be lovely. I miss the old times, hearing the lassie’s laugh, getting together.      Aye! They're all grown up now, you remember, but I still pop in once in a while. Mind you, I don’t know what's left of mine. Gave her the house, but that was years ago.      Blimey. Look at you, giving property! Me? I still live in Costessey—same ’ouse for over forty years.      Sounds good to me. No fancy modern developments uprooting your roots like I'm seeing all over town.      And always in the wrong place, too! They’re building some fancy housing estate right by the old primary school.      They think they’re clever, don’t they? But I say to them, who on earth wants to live where the school once stood?

So do you lot actually know what’s going to be in the AQA biology paper this time?      No one knows. Exam boards just love leaving us blind, don’t they?      I heard they’re focusing more on evolution and ecosystems. But who knows if that’s even real or just something someone said on an exam revision group on Reddit.      Online groups are full of rubbish. I got this theory from someone online about how humans started evolving from fish because of climate change and now we’re all going back underwater. Apparently, it’s in the next update of the spec.      Classic. All we need is a few conspiracy theorists on the internet and the whole school panicking. I swear my cousin’s partner tried to tell her the Moon Landing was faked, and now I hear it from her. Like, she was  there , for god’s sake, and now she’s second guessing everyone!      It’s the age we live in, innit? Everyone thinks they know more than experts now. I mean, do you see how girls in our class get treated sometimes? If you even mention evolution to some people, they act like it’s an attack on their beliefs.      Speak for yourself. Not all of us are clueless. I actually read up on natural selection and stuff. Let me tell you, it’s wild how something as simple as a beak shape can change an entire species over hundreds of years.      Yeah, but it's not just science we’re dealing with—look at the way some people still think girls can’t be as good at physics as boys. My cousin got pulled up about it at school. Just because she’s the only one in her year doing physics and a girl, they thought she was there to “make up numbers.”      That’s ridiculous. Everyone should just stick to what they can do, not based on what they look like or what they wear. I mean, some of the best nerds I know are girls. We had this one girl in our math class doing calculus in like two steps. No one believed it was her.      Still, it’s amazing how viral some of the random videos can go. I saw this thing about suffragettes where they got it completely wrong. Like, they said it was all about voting, but it’s about a lot more than that.

Rather skip the new tablet and go for the acupuncture, Joan. My sister had her sinus infections sorted with it... no side effects, just pain temporarily.      Erm, Joan, that's probably not the same with your operation. Look, the doctor says these tablets'll help with the infection site and prevent it from getting worse. You shouldn’t skip meds just for something like needles.      Oh, love, but I know someone from my knitting group who had a hip replacement and swore by the acupuncture. She said it was like the pain just... melted away, don't you know.      That sounds mostly like made-up stories me old girl. I had back complaints for years and they gave me a good old jab in the kidney and left it at that. Probably need to stick to what the doctors say, and I think they gave you a straight-forward prescription for that infection.      Absolutely, Greg. Now, are you alright for the MOT at the garage, love?      Erm, the lorry? That's gone, like ten years into retirement, luv. I mean, the van I used for deliveries is as dead as the dodo bird, but the motorhome? It's had new tyres. Still needs a services check, mind. Lady at the petrol station said the mot was still looming.      Let me remind you of the rugby weekend next month, will I? I already told Liam at the garage, and he's going to squeeze in an MOT and check the oil before we leave. He's been doing a discount for friends recently.      Oh, and skiing next month – I told your granddaughter, Laura, she reckons she's never been to the slopes. But she said she's keen to try. I suppose you and Jackie will know that better than me.      Definitely, that’s something to plan for. Maybe we can get her started at Nordicski – I heard they have a beginners’ programme. And as for the family, I spoke to my little ones today. They’re really looking forward to seeing Greg’s old photos from when he was a lorry driver.      Wasn’t that a laugh delivering the furniture with a dog in the back of the lorry? I remember it nearly suffocated once – poor lad.      Oh, don’t go on about that – it was your fault for letting the PSU have it in the first place, and then forgetting to lock those bloody cages.

Right, so today in History class, we started talking about slavery. I know it's such a heavy topic, but it's important to learn about, don’t you think?      What's slavery?      Hmm… Well, it's when one group of people make another group of people work for them without letting them go, and they treat them unfairly. It used to happen a long time ago, especially when European countries were exploring new places, like Africa and America.      Was it like… people were taken away from their homes?      Yes, exactly. Many people from Africa were taken by force and made to work on big plantations across the sea. They had no choice, no freedom, and they were treated badly. It was a crime, and now we try to learn from it and say sorry for the history of it.      That sounds really sad. Why would grown-ups do that?      That’s a really good question. People used to think that some people weren’t worthy of freedom, based on where they were from, the way they looked, or what their background was. It’s not okay, and we don’t live like that today — but we still need to fight against any kind of unfairness.      Mate… I don’t get it. If it was wrong, why did the people who did it not get in trouble?      Oh, that’s a tough one. For a long time, people in charge weren’t making the rules to protect those who were enslaved. It took many years and brave people—some of them former slaves and their families—to speak out and campaign against it. Eventually, laws were created to stop it.      Did other countries do it too?      Yes, many places around the world had slave systems. Even some in Europe. But, like I said, it ended because people started to see it for what it was — a huge wrong.      Was there war about it too?      Actually, yes. In the United States of America, there was a big war called the Civil War partly because of the difference between the northern and southern states on the issue of slavery. The southern states wanted to keep it, while the north wanted to stop it.      Oh, no! That's really bad.      It certainly was. But it goes to show how much of a problem it was and how long it took to fix.      So… what can we do now to help?

Right, I just wanted to bring up the whole thing about that new series on iPlayer,  Only Lovers Left on the Bus . Have you all seen it?      Oh yes, I’ve watched a couple of episodes. It’s not half as bad as  Bridgerton . Got a bit obsessed there for a while. My wife and I were watching it every night.      I haven’t seen  Only Lovers...  but I’m interested. Is it romantic comedy or drama?      A bit of both, honestly. It’s set in Bristol and reminds me of the sort of people who used to come through the ward when I worked night shifts. You know the type — always a bit quirky, living for the eccentric life. It makes me nostalgic, to be honest.      I think it’s just a flimsy excuse to show off Bristol’s skyline. I’ve been there twice this year. They’ve got a new café on the bottom of Queen Square that’s pretty good if you’re ever in the area, Anne.      Oh, I hope we can all get up there for a weekend trip soon. We might take the dog.      Oh, speaking of the dog. Mr. Beaky got into the recycled bottle bin again. I swear he doesn’t like plastic bottles, but he tears through the paper ones like it’s nothing.      That dog is a menace! I had a collie once, someone said he was part terrier. That creature was a nightmare.      Some people still watch the news, right? I thought it was intense this week — the whole situation in the Middle East.      Yes, I try to keep up as a nurse. There’s a lot of talk at work about how the global climate is affecting things like disease patterns. It’s quite worrying.      My sister’s son passed his A-Levels and now he’s trying to get into Med School. He says there’s no way you can understand half the references in the biology text unless you’ve followed the climate debate for years.      That poor kid. I took the copywriting course where they expect you to be familiar with everything from Kafka to K-pop. It’s brutal.      Just don’t expect me to follow, luv. I like the boxset binges and the Financial Times crossword. That’s as far as it goes.      As long as the crossword makes sense, I suppose. Just don’t fall asleep over the kettle again like last time!

Right, who’s up for helping me unload the dishwasher? I think it’s your team’s turn this week...         Ew, dirty plates? I don’t wanna!      But it’s  my  turn!           Both of you are on the same team. You’ve got to work together or I’ll make you read a whole chapter of  Harry Potter  instead.      Ugh, okay. But only the easy bits.      Yeah, skip the parts where people die.      Oh, don’t worry, we’ll stop at the good bit where they go on the train. But you boys – I’m watching you.      I think I read somewhere that George Stephenson was the first person to invent something really, really cool. Wasn’t he like... the inventor of trains?      No, you didn’t read that. That was my  brother , not you.      Well, listen老爷! I read it yesterday in a book from the library and everything.      Actually… he wasn't  the  inventor, but yes, he was one of the most important people in making trains work properly. He’s called the “father of railways.” It was back in the 1800s, and he designed the first steam railway.      That’s so old! Like, like a time before smartphones.      Yeah, but he did science and machines and stuff, so maybe if he had a smartphone, he would’ve made about five billion apps.      Oh come  on , you couldn’t even  imagine  a smartphone back then.      You’re both right to some extent, but for someone who lived in Geo’s time, he was a total genius. He made the world faster – before cars, planes, or even trams.      So, you mean if he were alive now, he’d probably invent the lunches we keep forgetting to take out the freezer?         That man would’ve invented go-karts on pond water if you asked him.      You’re both making me proud. Although the go-karts on pond water one sounds dodgy. Alright, who’s fetching the cleaning towel? We’ve got a tea towel soaked in dry shampoo over there to wipe up the mess from last night’s spaghetti.      I’m not wiping my finger near that. I once saw a spider in there.      I did not need to hear that now. I was just starting to like your house!         Right, then, tea towels are  Mum’s  job – but you two? You're still dish-duty duty. Now, who wants to hold the pepper pot?

Right, I just texted Jess to see if she fancied coming over for supper club tomorrow night. We could do the whole ‘home-cooked dining experience’ vibe. You know, like those fancy supper clubs where it’s just £20 a head and you serve people in your kitchen in East London. Got eeny weeny crockery?      Ay, I’m all in. Though I reckon I only have enough flatware to feed a family of five. Oh, and my oven is currently as dead as a man in the heatwave. So I’ll probably just be the glorified carvery fetcher, passing you baked potatoes and hoping no one notices the static cheese slices I’ve got stuck to the side of the turkey.      Och, no worries. I’ll bring the bread and the lemon curd and I’ll be the little ‘Oooh, aren’t these scones breakfast, lunch and brunch?’. Should be enough to fool inquisitive dinner guests. Also, I thought I’d bring some spare crockery. One time, I once hosted a dinner for ten, and I used my cat’s bowl as a serving plate. Bless him, he didn’t even notice his colouring had changed for a week.      Be serious. You’re a baker – surely you have at least one porcelain plate that isn’t covered in flour. Though, honestly, maybe the rustic aesthetic would work in our favour. “Come one, come all, to our very posh East London Spaghetti & Adjacent Catastrophe Supper Club!”      Mate, I’d be there with a truffle and a tea towel. I’ve had enough posh evenings in Sydney to know how to spin chaos into charm. “Ah, the pass is chaotic tonight – but it’s all part of the experience.” Not that I’ve ever worked in a ‘posh’ restaurant. But I tried to rebrand my guest speaker event at the barista college as “A curated sensory journey” – it was just me trying to spell ‘latte art’ without getting distracted by the drip filter.      Websites mentioned earlier – do any of you know what the ‘Words With Friends’ app actually  does ? I’ve had it downloaded for years, but it just sits there on my phone, like a social reminder of my preoccupied college years. I’m not entirely sure if it’s a game, a bonding experience, or a ghosting accessory.      You open it, you start with the word ‘bee’ and then you just sit there for two hours wondering if the C and the T you added actually form a word.

Rather skip the queue and take a sandwich from the office fridge. I blame you for starting it.      Never mind them. I’m more interested in football. I've been into that a lot lately.      That's brilliant! Have you been watching the Euros much?      Yeah, I try to catch as much as I can. I actually have been going a bit wild with betting too. Not that I'd tell my uncle Tim; he’d go mad.      You and betting, sounds like a fun chase when it's not draining your pay packet, like it tends to.      All in the name of excitement, really. You like that sort of thing?      No, not really. I’m far too safety-focused for anything like that. If I wanted to blow my hard-earned, I’d do it on breakfast, not betting.      Haha, fair point. I'm the complete opposite — I blow it on cakes and books. I've actually been baking more since I moved into my flat a couple of months ago. Got a bit of a baking bug.      Baking? Tell me you’re not watching those GIRL Genie baking shows again. You’re bound to come out with a new hobby every week.      Okay, fair enough. Now don’t go making fun when I show up with a Russian sourdough rye loaf and you’re still someone who eats Tesco’s suspiciously soft white bread.      I buy what feeds my kid at a reasonable price and doesn’t take an hour to make. I don’t have time for most hobbies about now. My main hobby is pretending I know what the hell I’m doing most days — what with this job and trying to keep two kids out of trouble.      My, you are multi-tasking. Do you manage much spare time for yourself at all?      If I write it down, I somehow manage it. You know, time blocks. Try it, and maybe you won’t live off pizza and takeaways all the time.      Haha, well you remember delivering pizza around this very building years ago. Don’t go getting all smug on me.      True, I do remember, but that was before I had a bloke who complained about your dodgy service. I have grown up, apparently.      From dodgy service to dodgy betting addiction to dodgy mothering, sound about right.      Something like that. I might be dodgy at all those things, but I can still make a mean Victoria sponge.

So do you think we got everything off the list, grans? I know I got the loo rolls... got the big ol’ pack of lavatory paper and I got a few cleaning things.      Not quite love. Look, we’ve still got to get the baby wipes and that eeny weeny bottle of apple juice for the little one. Oh, and I wanted to check if they’ve got that big purple blanket we saw in the window. The one with the sheep on it, you know?      That one’s me favourite when it come out. Tore me heart out to see it cost twenty fiver. But me daughter went and bought it for me for me birthday like that.      Oh! Yeah I remember you mentioned that, grans. You looked at it like it was the Queen’s crown. Blimey, twenty pounds? That better last a lifetime.      Honestly, I only bought it because I felt like it was worth it, even if it is a bit overpriced. But that’s retail for you, isn’t it? I mean, I work in a shop quite a bit, and you’d think they’d knock prices down a bit if they live near them.      Aye, but that’s business, innit? I think it’s all about the branding. You know, apple juice and sheep and all that. If I was ‘im, I’d put a tiger on it just to scare people into buying it.      Hahaha, yeah or put out a ‘cool kid’ branded blanket and say it comes with a DJ license.      Not a bad idea actually... Maybe I’ll pitch it to the marketing team at mine job. Though I suppose you’re not meant to be selling retail ideas in the housing office.      That’s for the bloke in guest service like me, not for people with brains like you lot.      Oh, I dunno, grans. I’m going to uni in a few months, but I reckon if you’ve got a plan and the big purple blanket with sheep, you can work any job.      That’s the spirit! Just remember to get your degree, your degree, your degree. But also, line your walls with sheep blankets.      Aye, and don’t forget to have a big cot to go with it, mind.      Oh, grans, we talk about dolls and stuff, but we haven’t mentioned this drastic new baby yet...

So do you lot ever actually go out anymore, or is everyone just glued to their phones and laptops?      Ah love, I’m more of a radio kind of gal now. Keeps me company while I knit. What about you, Adam?      Honestly, most of the time I’m just playing this one game online with mate. It’s basically all I do these days.      Which one? I’ve got to play something with my bro over the holidays.      It’s like this survival RPG— Elden Ring . You get like, miniature castles and monsters and everything. Bit intense, but addictive, you know?      Survival games? I remember playing  The Sims  when I was young. It was the closest I ever got to being in charge of someone’s life!      Yeah, I still play that sometimes. I mean, not the old one, the new one. Mega boring compared to, you know, actual games where you fight stuff.      Fair point, but it’s relaxing. Not everything has to be a battle royale to be fun.      Maybe. I just reckon the brain needs rhythm and stimulus. Like how we studied psychology at uni—isn't it said that routine is death to the mind?      Mate, you just finished uni. If what you learned is that routine kills the mind, then you’ve got a full house.      Laughter, Adam, that's the mood you should all be focused on. You can’t be stressing over microbes and psychological theories when it’s nearly Christmas.      I’m not stressing, I just found it interesting. Honestly, it made me question why I even like playing games. Is it to avoid stress, or to create some sense of achievement that we don’t get elsewhere?      Both? Like, the whole dopamine hit? It's science, right?      I don't know about science, but I know what  I  like: the lunches we have on Christmas Day! My nan’s roasted meats…  chef’s kiss .      That is good. Though I think nan is about to start lecturing me on travel next—if I mention Australia again, I might be in trouble.      Why’s that?      Because apparently, after I go, I can never come back, and she’s expected me to visit every year since I was five.      Typical! The holidays are for going away, the rest of the year is for coming back, love.      To be fair, though, it’s not like there’s much work left in this place.

Okay, so today we're talking about metals and fabrics, right? I was just reading about iron, cotton... What do you kids know about them?      I know iron is for swords in Minecraft! And cotton makes beds and stuff.      And diamonds make the best sword! I got a diamond sword last weekend when I played with Dad!      Well yes, diamonds are amazing in Minecraft, but in real life, iron and cotton are super useful, too. Iron is one of the strongest metals. It's used for building, cars, even things like your toys' wheels. Cotton is mostly used for clothes. It’s soft and keeps us warm or cool, depending on how it’s made.      Can we make cotton into pretend blankets?      Of course! In the real world, you can, but we can do better here. What if we turn this into a game? You can be inventors creating new legendaries! Maybe, you know, a magical fabric that stops flames or a metal that helps you jump higher?      I want a metal that makes your sword as strong as a diamond sword in Minecraft!      Good thinking! But what about other metals? You’ve heard of iron, maybe steel? Steel is even stronger than iron and is used in bridges and skyscrapers.      Is steel what the big bridges are made of? Like the Tower Bridge?      Yes! That’s right. It’s one of the strongest materials out there. Also, have you heard of bronze and copper? They were used in ancient times to make tools and weapons long before steel.      But what about silver? I have a thimble that’s shiny like it.      Silver is a beautiful metal and has some special uses. It’s good for electronics because it conducts electricity really well. And it can be made into jewellery or tableware. Speaking of, I take a silver vitamin every day. It’s supposed to good for your immunity.      Do metals taste like the vitamins?      Vitamins are fake metal, though. They’re in the pill.      Not fake metal – just minerals made into a tablet. But yes, they’re good for your body, just like your vegetables. Now, how about fabrics? You know cotton, and there’s wool, silk, and linen. Silk is from silkworms and is super smooth. Linen is made from flax plants and feels really cool in the summer.      I like my wool scarf. It keeps me warm in the winter.      Exactly.

So did y’all hear about this EPQ thing? My teacher’s been going on about it like it’s the be-all and end-all of sixth form. Me and me bro went to Wembley Arena last year to a concert but it was breakfast, no Bucks Fizz this time.      Blooming hell, is that what they’re serving nowadays?      Mate, that tour was one of the most controversial things I’d ever seen. I mean, some people said it was brilliant, and others thought it was ... well ... odd.      Well, it got more folk out than the Queen’s speech, I reckon, and that’s saying something considering she’s the Queen. Now don’t get me started on the Queen. I watched one of them old BBC documentaries on her childhood and I couldn’t help but think—what if she didn’t like being Queen?      Honestly, I find her fascinating. Not the being Queen bit, but the  idea  of it. Like, how did that whole system even start? I mean, the monarchy is like an ancient institution and yet it still lingers on.      Dude, we went over that in history, ‘cos of the whole National Poverty thing after the Industrial Revolution. The Crown kept them folk in line by holding on to all them titles and estates. It’s a little mad, honestly.      You bloke, you always talk like that. I mean, whot do you do when you want to be productive, after a day of arguing with the system? J go out and get your own place and start cookin’?      Actually, I’m thinking of doing a vegetarian cookbook when I leave all this behind. It’d focus on recipes from countries with high rates of poverty where cheap, local ingredients are key.      Oh, that’s mad.

Honestly, I don't know how anyone expects us to live on this budget. I paid for groceries this week and got nothing out of it—literally just a box of oats and a loaf of toast bread.      You're not the only one being ripped off, Lizz. I tried to get a fiver out of my mom today for the bus and she gave me the  I'm-a-hard-working-mum-and-you're-being-unreasonable  look. I told you to move in with the twins. Emily actually sends her mum a shop list and she delivers it every Wednesday. Like, takes care of two students out of guilt or something. I'm real jealous.      You reckon I should ask my nan then? She sends me money every week but it's always wrapped in paper and stuff because she’s scared of banks or something. She says it's “safe” but it was the same amount as a loaf of bread, which I then used to make chicken Tikka Masala with because my energy bill is just flying out the window.      Chicken Tikka Masala and being cold at the same time? That’s a special set of circumstances, mate. I’m eating the same bhangra chips my dad packed for me from home. There's not much variety but at least I’m not hungry. And  slight accent shift  yeah, for the record, bhangra chips are spicy, salty, and have been approved as a meal by yours truly.      Honestly, I’m just getting spooned out by life at the moment. I’ve had to move out with my girlfriend for the whole of next term because I can’t afford the additional night light in my room anymore. Rather skip the new DVD till Boxing Day innit, me and mine are meeting her nan and they’re like... got the big telly with the sky and everything. I can watch it all      Right. So we'll see the film when we get back from Cornwall?      Yeah, sounds good. I told the lass I'd pick her up as well. Though I said I'd pick her up just before one from my nan's. I've got the turkey in the oven and I've got to think of the kids and I've got to think of the dog and I've got to think of the..." and I was thinking "Crikey, what if you actually forgot about the turkey?"      You need to just remember to laugh off the pressure at the end of the day. That's what I do.      Yeah, that's what I do tell her lass, I say, listen I don't care about your mum's turkey. I only care about having a good time.      Absolutely. Be like the way it used to be when we were kids. I remember my mam making the star anise tea the other night and telling me to just enjoy the whole season.      That's right, the old days.      And you know what? It just felt oddly therapeutic.      I think the secret to Christmas being successful is just having good people to be with. You know, about five or six years back I had such a good Christmas. We were down in Exeter doing some work at a language school and then I invited some friends down. We went out to the market, had a little drink and ended up meeting someone at the bar who ended up inviting me to a party in a surf shop. Wild.      You must have met some interesting people back then.      Oh yeah, people from all over the place—Dubai, the Americas, even a bloke who worked with tigers in the Sahara.      That's wild.      I just started smiling when I thought about it the other day. You know what your face looks like when you're planning something and you're just like, "Oh my god, I think I’m going to get to do it sometime soon."

Dad, thanks for coming all this way. I know it’s a bit of a trek, especially with everything that’s changed in the roads around here now.      It’s no problem, son. Though I have to say, the speed cameras are getting more than a bit thick — if it wasn’t for my  new  license, I’d be on holiday in the Caymans instead of with a clean record!      Haha, true. Oh, and you   have   got to watch out for that roundabout near the depot. Looks the same but the exit has changed — almost like someone filmed a scene from  Mission: Impossible  there.      That bad, eh? Anyway, how are you? Still teaching?      Yeah, I’m in my second year now. The school’s doing alright. It helps that about half the students are here to brush up for university entrance exams in Anglophone countries — Americans especially.      That sounds serious. You working too hard?      Sometimes. I do take the weekend off, though. Though I might take a break longer than that to go to Tanzania with some colleagues. Have you ever been?      Tanzania, like the one with the Great Migration?      Yeah, Serengeti and the like. I’ve been telling them to pack layers — you never know what the weather’s doing at that time of year.      Sounds grand. Just don’t forget a good book for the long flight. Some people still watch  Game of Thrones  over and over, but a decent board game passes time as well.      That trip does sound like the right one to take  Catan  — or whatever they call it now. Not that I’d beat you, Dad.       Haha ! You always had high hopes, didn’t you? Just remember to take it easy on the fresh fruit there.      You mean I could get sick from mangoes and end up being the joke of the trip?      Well, I’ve seen it happen. Still, I’m proud of you. Moving out to Brighton must go against everything I taught you about staying close to home and avoiding beach cities!      It wasn’t a big move — just the train from Bedford’s longer than I expected. But it’s bright and open there, and cheap enough, I’ll say that. Less racism than some places, from what I’ve seen.      You know my take on that. Always stand up for yourself and don’t let anyone twist your words. Right place, wrong reasons.

Rather skip the new barista café near the station, anyone fancy a coffee run after this?      I’ll take one of those, thank you. Not had a proper break all week, and I’m starting to feel it. Was it the one on the corner near the Haberfield site?      Yeah, that one. I reckon it’s got all the PR buzz a place needs — listing ethics, Fair Trade, this and that. I jest, I’ll grab a small flat white with oat milk if they do it. You’ve already got the left-hand side of the kitchen covered, I’ll do the bin and pick up the dry cleaning.      You’ve got to stop calling breakfast cleaning, whatever that means. Just remember to put the lights on at the shop, and pick up that shopping list from the spare room laptop. I made a note: 'Stick to practical music resources for the kids'. That way, fewer chaotic drum solos. I’m thinking flutes, keyboards, whatever won’t break the floorboards.      You’re forgetting most kids about to fall off the walls don’t need the Renaissance flute — they want электрические гитары. But I know you’re worrying about acoustics.      And the noise. Our guest speaker last month had to cancel his session at 6 a.m. because some student insisted on rehearsing their pop song at 2. I’m still being billed for that.      He probably just wanted to keep the momentum from the night before — the one he’d set after delivering a 3-hour course on the Romantic era. He looked rather smug, if you ask me.      I’ll let that slide because we were both blooming tired from the train after Brighton. So, post-supper, perhaps we can listen to some violin sonatas to drown out the marching band from across the street? I’ve been over this so much I’m surprised I still string a sentence together.

Rather annoying isn't it? The water just seeps through. I've had it for ages.      I know what you mean. It's been drooping by the toilet for weeks now. I was thinking we should do something about it.      Yeah, we should get a new shower curtain. Maybe even paint the bathroom while we’re at it. It’s starting to look a bit dated. Well, it’ll be a great place to put his treats. A little fabric pouch on the side, something like that.      That's a good idea. I can add velcro to one side so we can open and close it.      If we’re already doing the bathroom and the bean bag, what about starting on the evening meal? Let's not wait too long. I thought we could do spaghetti with a tomato-chilli sauce. Then we can tackle the bathroom together while it's still dry on the outside if you don’t mind painting.      I don’t mind at all, I just need to finish your supper first! Rather annoying this, isn't it? You think they'd have everything sorted by internet by now.      What's the matter now, dear? I can hear the frustration      It's that blasted pension form, I got one today — you know the one from the government? Seems I've missed something from the 'sixties. I reckon it was when I was in the merchant navy. A lot of things got lost in the wars, if you know what I mean.      Oh no, not the national insurance contribution chase again. I had that too not too long ago. It said I couldn’t qualify because I missed two years and I had only six working quarters in a decade My son had to help me with it. He’s a qualified accountant! I didn’t know what half of it meant. I think he turned 14 while assembling it      I envy you that then — I mean, not the lack of pension, the help. I haven’t got no child to do it. Just me and this dog, Sid, taking himself for walks and looking at me like I’m deranged when I mutter about NI numbers to myself.         Speak of the dog, here – Mate, I got the dog, and he's just chewed up my old paper somethin’ awful.         That’s your business sense huh? Our Sid just likes to destroy things with meaning. That government form? It counts for less than a shoe with a hole in it now.      I still don’t get why they can't make it simple about this. I worked for the same company from 1972 to ’98. There was no leaves of absence, no gaps. I even kept a scrapbook of my pay stubs.      You did? That’s more dedicated than I could ever be. I sent mine off as it was, I tried to do it all on the computer but the form didn't like that. It kept saying 'invalid entry' but I was just writing what I was asked         Did you use the 'date of employment' field on your own birthday again by mistake      Is it? I might have. I wrote ‘1993’ one time and the system popped up with, “Are you sure you want to submit a start date after your year of retirement?” I thought it was some kind of over-enthusiastic chatbot      The worst part is, they don’t ring you or anything.

So did you manage to sort out that weekend trip with your mates then, Lizzie?      Yeah, well sort of. I’m going down to Brighton with them on the 23rd, but I’m only staying a night and then heading home on the 24th. Got a meeting the next morning.      Still, better than not going at all, I reckon. A change is as good as a rest, isn’t it, Angela?      If it’s Brighton, I don’t see how it could get worse. Still buzzing from the time we went down last year! Spent so much money, but the sea air was worth it.      Haha, you always talk like that on the way home, Ange. But yes, a short break might be just the thing for you, Lizzie. How’s your gig with the breakfast radio show coming along?      Oh, don’t remind me. I’m doing a Christmas special next week and the host is driving me insane. He keeps asking for "quotidian" Christmas tunes and says "everyone wants culture in their festive cheer". It’s either  The Nutcracker  or  Les Mis  for the jingles this year.      Oh no, not another artsy Christmas special. I just want  Jingle Bells  and maybe a bit of  Run Silly Sleigh .      Honestly, I prefer the traditional stuff. Nothing wrong with  Fairytale of New York  either, to be fair.      Well, as long as you’re still getting paid for your sanity, Lizzie. I about lost mine doing the day shift at the clinic the week before Christmas last year. Half of what you hear at that time of year is barely a tune it is a  moan .      Poetic, Nurse Julie.      Come on, don’t let her ruin your Christmas spirit. We’ll meet up for a little pre-Christmas drink. Saturday? Just like we do every year.      Yeah, speaking of which, have we organised the food? Still veggie for the main, or are you going to cave in and do the normal stuff this year, Steve?      I’ll cave in if Ange does the box set one again. I can’t do vegan pigs in blankets again.      Oh, come on! They were delicious!      I for one am very grateful we’ve stopped arguing over the turkey. Searing my arm last year was enough for me.      And remember, once, Steve, when you tried to thaw the turkey in the microwave?      That was last century! And besides, I had my reasons.

Rather do I though.      That is surprising. I thought her former would be in like.      Oh it is like more than I can take.      It is.      Look I mean as frightened as I am about it I also want eeny weeny bit of excitement in my life.      I know.      A lot of people would think that this is a funny story but it is not.      What you mean was she.      She was the most amazing animal trainer I like to think of even now.      What the people who drink.      My turkey.      Your what.      My Turkey.      Eww.      It is now dead.      What.      He has a microchip he goes everywhere with me ever since 2008.      What did he do that.      Nothing.      I mean if you lost your Turkey to a credit card Turkey then something is wrong in the fabric of reality.      He just got left in the taxi.      He got left.      I had a new flat in London and my next door neighbour who was a film producer invited me for mexican chicken and then in this someone who found one of the two dogs which my ex.      I think what you mean is your ex's dog and then the other dog got run over.      Yeah.      That is not you.      I had to document it on camera and make a documentary that was like barely a week.      That was your idea.      To put my dog on camera with his health condition.      But he was fine he had spinal surgery.      Yeah but the surgery didn't go that well.      And that is a new fact.      Yeah he's lost his legs.      Oh.      I mean it was supposed to be.      Is it fake legs.      No he lost his legs due to a spinal infection at the age of 13 and then he's had replacement surgery so he regenerated some of his legs to like.      Yeah so why not be surprised that you ended up with a Turkey instead of a dog.      I don't know it always happens.      Oh now that is funny.      Yeah before.      So then what did you name your Turkey.      Steve.      Steve.      Yeah it was just a joke.      Why the name.      Because he looked like Steve the Tourist or something.      Oh so your Turkey looked like Steve the Tourist and then the dog looked like Steve the Tourist.      Yeah they were.      That is genuinely horrifying.      That is what I'm saying.

Rather skip the new bar and go through the park, don't you think? The air out here feels like... I don’t know, slightly toxic. It’s not even midday yet, and you can feel that hazy smog in your throat.      You’re right, it’s awful. I noticed it on the walk to work this morning too. Someone joked that it’s "air quality like you’ve never felt before." Not exactly reassuring. I wonder if it's a sandstorm from the Gobi or just Beijing’s usual cloud of "mystery particles."      Probably a bit of everything, honestly. Still, I made sure to grab my mask this morning, and I’ve been trying to keep the windows closed all day. I swear my throat’s a dustbin by the time I get home. It’s getting to the point where the pollution feels like an added job — a really frustrating one.      I know what you mean. I spent part of the lunch hour Googling air quality indexes to see if it was even safe to walk outside for more than ten minutes. My colleague joked that we’d all start gliding instead of walking to avoid as much contact with the dirt.      Honestly, sometimes I feel like we should be paid just for breathing. How much does that add to burnout, right? Dealing with toxic air, plus the commute, plus trying to be professional lecturers at universities? It's already tough enough dealing with the curriculum and the endless feedback loops — but breathing shouldn't cost you a second opinion from a pulmonologist.      Also, it's the uncertainty. You don’t know whether it’s chemicals from the factories or just someone’s exhaust. I mean, I love this city, and the job is great, but I can’t shake this constant worry. Every time you see a kid playing near a busy road without a mask... it’s heartbreaking. I keep thinking about how my parents are going to react when they come to visit. They told me they brought jackets, but I think they need masks too.      Ugh, that’s what I was thinking earlier. I’ve been planning little “safe zones” for their visit. Like, where they can walk around with the mask on the least amount of go-to hell on Earth. I’ve even suggested indoor walking tours in air-filtered shopping malls. Hopefully, they'll go with it — though I suspect your dad will swear he doesn’t need a mask and insist he’s “built tough.”

Rather skip the newfit meat again. You know what I mean. I had it last time and it was a bit on the dry side.      I know what you mean. It's a bit mealy. Not quite up to the same standard as the good old Butler’s or whatever. Got eeny plans for lunch yet?      I reckon I might try something different today. I’ve been craving some proper flatbreads. Laksa made that last Sunday, didn’t it, love? You know the one that Myra grows. You’ve met Myra left?      Yeah, I remember her. Rather picky about what she waters and what she doesn’t, by the looks of it. I see her every now and then in town, she always in there at the market planting her stalls.      She's a proper green-fingered one that one. I do tell you.      Yeah I reckon if we went round as a group she might even give us a few extra sprigs.      That would be nice. So is that what we doing then: Bread, mozzarella and basil it is?      Doesn't sound bad to me. I might pop on the film ‘Balenciaga and the Lost Years’ in the background. Spotted it on the telly this morning. It's one I haven’t seen yet.      Sounds like a good plan. I’ve been watching loads of those documentary shows on the telly. Not quite the same as eating round the table together though, is it.      No, it isn’t. I’d say it is a proper tonic to come home and eat like that. I’ve been at the hospital all day, you know. Just me and the sirens for company mainly. I had a bit of a sprained wrist earlier today doing some lifting, didn’t I?      Did you? That’s a right pain in the backside if you let it go for too long.      I’ve put some goop on it and it’s getting better though. Just got to be careful not to overdo it between now and the box day.      Cos you don’t want to miss it all on day two, do you? I heard it gets even better as it goes on.      Yeah, the food and the fitting together both.

Have you heard about the new bus route?      No, what’s it up to?      It’s supposed to connect the train station more directly to the main uni campus, but I’ve only seen a few prototype posters up so far. They’re timing it to coincide with the start of term, I think.      That's actually really welcome, I reckon. A lot of people would love that—especially if it’s easier to get into town without pulling out the clanger of a timetable change.      Definitely. Still, I heard a lot of students complaining online already. Someone apparently saw a sign-up at the Cambridge University Press bookshop about needing more volunteers to protest it.      Oh right? Why, is the bus going to replace some of the existing routes or something?      Yeah, they’re scrapping the old 6 and 8 routes, which some tutors apparently use to get to the colleges in the mornings, even though those routes are a bit clunky. One bloke was overheard saying he’s had to take a cab twice already this week.      Honestly, welcome to Cambridge. You’ve got to be a bit of a rhythm reader when it comes to local transport here.      Right? I mean, I’m used to the messiness of public transport, but Cambridge throws its own curveballs. Last week, I saw a student dressed as a squirrel someone said was one of the protesteers from the bookshop action.      A squirrel? Seriously? That’s either really creative activism or a prank.      Kinda both, honestly. They waved a sign that just said,  “Take the bus… or be squirrel.”       I mean, it does sound a bit like the kind of protest culture you get at Oxford too. Though at Oxford, their activists just handed out tote bags.      Oh, I hear they did a little performance art piece involving a giant inflatable tutu.      That’s… Oxfordian. At least they do things with style.      Don’t get me started on their grass verges—ever seen pond life staging a civil disobedience? I think I saw a goose in a tutu.      You might have misheard that. I’m pretty sure it was a conference seminar, not pond life. Oxford can be full of eccentrics like that. Whereas here, over half the protests are about parking permits.      I think that's Cambridge Confidential.      Makes you wonder if we should compare uni experiences. I mean, I hear they’re into academics at Oxford before social shenanigans, but here, you can start a protest on a Tuesday and still be at a pub quiz on a Wednesday.

So did you talk to him yet?      Talk to who, love?      You know, Liam—Michael’s boyfriend. The one coming up for the weekend?      Oh, aye. That one. He seems a nice enough lad from what you two told me. Still, I don’t like the idea of him coming over without a full stomach.      What do you mean? We told him we’d be going out for lunch in Cheshire. This is just you andMichael having the house to yourselves for a while before the chaos starts.      Aye,  if  I get to choose the menu, there won't be any chaos. My turkey and broccoli quiche recipe hasn’t left anyone in tears yet. I made it for the Oliver family, and Elinor gave me six stars— gold  stars, mind you.      You need to stop thinking like a maths teacher, Aisling. Liam is 29, not a Year 7 student. He won’t expect you to score him.      Although, now I think of it, your dishes did end up in a food competition once. Didn’t they launch something on TikTok because of it?      Aye, that’s what happens when you’re still living off the Hayfields’ leftovers. The daughter set up a page calling them “Grandma Nourish’s Mid-Century Medleys.” Honestly, I just wanted to make sure the girls got a balanced meal after their mam’s hangover stew.      I think the internet would want more of that stew, actually.      Not today, thanks. I’m eating for two now, and the smell of “mam’s cooking” can make me faint. Don’t you remember the time we helped clean up after her “carrot fudge” attempt?      A tragedy for all involved. But anyway, the point is, Liam will be fine. Just don’t let him near your macaroons again. Last time, he thought they were  cookies , not  fancy French pastries  with digestive values like he’d swallowed a dictionary.      He was just being polite. He didn’t really need to analyse every bite like it was a thesis topic.      Polite or not, he ate one and went on a 20-minute rant about the  texture资产负债表 and the roles of gluten in crust formation . I had to send him to the farm to see the “ingredient source” up close to shut him up.      I think that was brilliant, honestly. You’re both so old school.      Not us. Michael, and slightly Liam.

Rather skip the car and take the bus weekend to Wales, do we need one for the kids? Not nearly about them as about what I'd miss out on! But you're right, let’s not be too selfish. Going is better than staying.      Maybe we're not thinking big enough.
