But remind me, sometimes when I drive, it’s like I have to flu or something. Thought it’s not wise to push your luck.      Just talk about the plans over tea, why not? Make it like we're making it all up as we go.

Honestly, I don't know how you do it, Mum. Every day, just jumping out of bed like...  normal . I'm still half-dead from lectures and all I want to do is crawl back under the duvet with a blanket and Netflix.      Oh, I get it, Mollie, I used to be the same. But once you have kids—and two of them—it kind of pulls you out of bed before the alarm goes off, trust me.      Oh, and you think  this  is bad? Try getting out of bed with a wonky hip like I’ve got. I  managed  to get to the garden this morning before it rained and made that Myra look like a drowned rat.      Myra the bear? You're still into that? I remember her head falling off when you were, like, 8. Mum stitched it back on with sewing thread and some Elmer's glue.      She’s not  Myra , she’s  Myrrah  now, thank you very much. I gave her a full transformation—checked her out in the "Build a Bear" shop and everything.      Oh, for heaven's sake, give it a rest. She's 18 years old, evolving along with you, it's  horrifying .      Speaking of bears, will someone please tell me why Liam’s nursery teacher let him bring in a soft toy full of custard? I found my son clutching a soggy, yellow  Bah Humbug  at 3 in the afternoon and it poured out when I hugged him.      I  told  her not to let the little one near the “crunch and stuff” ones—he fails at potty training AND potty treats.      Well, at least he's trying. My Geo’s been passed out on the tiled floor at 6 a.m. holding something he insisted was the Eiffel Tower. It was just a plastic stick.      Auntie Myra always knows the best stories. I still remember the time you took Geo to the pond for his swimming lesson and nearly caused a flood the size of the gothic lake on your own if you tried to get into the deep end.      That wasn’t a  flood , that was just a  very large splash . The caretaker looked like he wanted to give me a ticket, I’ll admit, but I’ve had a life or two over this one.      Now that I think about it, Mollie, do you still use that old iPhone? You know the one that spontaneously goes into camera mode when you try to open the weather app, right before it drops a cold front on you.

So, I’ve been doing a fair bit of thinking since we got here, and it’s real easy to see how the time could just drift away while we're stuck in the same rhythm.      I know what you mean. That's kind of the point of house-sitting, isn’t it? To slow things down and take a breather. But maybe it's not all bad that it's making us reflect a little.      Exactly. And it makes me wonder—when you look ahead, what do you see? Not just short-term plans, but the big things you'd like to tick off in the next couple of years.      That's a heavy question to throw at me after lunch. But I guess I’d like to feel like I’m growing professionally, maybe take on some more responsibility at school or even start up a PD program for other teachers. What about you?      Fair. For me, I’ve been thinking about scaling the business in a way that doesn’t chew up so much of my time. I’d like to get into mentoring, maybe pass some of the day-to-day to someone else so I can focus on the bigger picture. Or even explore opportunities in education tech—it always interests me.      That sounds amazing. I know you’ve always wanted to leave a legacy beyond the business. I imagine mentoring would be quite rewarding, especially if you have a passion for building people up.      Yeah, someone recently put it to me that the most valuable investment a business leader can make is in people—whether that's employees, clients, or customers.      I like that. And it makes me think—have we ever talked about what our life looks like beyond this chapter? Not just in terms of work, but family-wise.      You mean like planning to have kids, settle down, the whole nine yards?      Something like that. You know, I was thinking the other day how it's easy for people to wait until the "perfect time." But what if we started doing a bit of planning? Just to keep the conversation from being so vague?      I’m happy with that. I think the tricky part is that we need to figure out what our priorities are so we can make space for the things that really matter. For example, if we're starting a family, we’ll need to have a much clearer idea of how we want to balance that with our careers.

Right, I swear I haven't seen anything so utter in ages. That lad in Costa, ‘ow much is this lot?’ with a vowel gap the size of Blighty. I was nearly in stitches!      Oh yeah, I saw what you mean. He looked like he hadn’t een a vocal lesson since the 80s!      Proper Wigan? I reckon. A lot worse than Aysh’s from Leeds, though. Oh but don’t get me started on that journey!      Oh come on, Aysh speaks perfectly. You just can’t abide decent vowels.      Look, the only way I can tell where someone’s from is if they say "bleedin’" left, right and centre! I ain’t obsessed, I’m just picky!      It is funny, though. ‘Ow’re ye doin’? I’m all righ’ in me basc’s’ and so on. Proper working class lingo. Should be bottled.      I know, you get it in service stations too. I swear if one more person asks me for a fag off me when I ain’t got one, I’ll...      You just say you’ve gone down the road to Freshney and ask if they’ve got some. Let’s be real.      You know what, ‘freshney road’ isn't even the name of someone who sells fags—just a cheeky way of avoiding the question.      Also, have you seen the way people here look at you if you smoke outside in broad daylight? Not in about five decades have they gone all "anti-fag lit" like this place.      Tell me about it. I left me Fitbit at home, but I do know, ‘cos every time I sneaked out for one, it was like I was in lockdown. I’d told me mate Tom I’d get him a pack, but he musta forgotten me.      Let’s not talk about Tom. I ain't heard from that one in weeks. Was going to camp with him, but he’s MIA! Maybe he's away goin' on some life mission like "fight or flight" or whatever.      Fight or flight, blooming hell! I’d just fly and go watch Pokémon again.      Oh, come on! Pokémon is basically like a life mission now. I saw that ‘Charizard’ one on TikTok this morning that looks like it’s been lasered at a theme park.      Ugh, I don’t get the appeal. I prefer remembering the old ways—probably when I played before social media, when Pokémon was just some paper cards you passed in the playground.

Rather skip the newfit lot eh?      Aye, it's such a mire of nonstop displays, ain't it? It's not like football in bygone days where we watched and it was just that.      But Granddad, things have evolved a bit. I mean, there  are  still good parts, but yeah, it's not all roses.      No, but I'll have this lot back to playing under a tree with a dented tin can. We had nothing and we were content.      That's a rather poetic image, but I think even you'd struggle to keep a team together with just a tin can and some enthusiasm now.      Yeah well, you boys and young lasses would never withstand a minute of it I reckon.      I was about to say something similar. I still remember taking care of this one lad, Matthew — only four at the time — and he’d chase a ball down the street and back again. Good for him.      My, yes! That must’ve been the 70s?      Oh goodness, yes. Harrow in '74. I'd trot over in a minibus with half a dozen children — it was mostly just me, and sometimes a volunteer or two. Some of them were quite cheeky, mind you.      And some were angelic — like yours truly in this group — full of charm and mischief.      Hardly. Some lecturers are more playful than others, I imagine.      I bet you are! You two have about you that university smartness — you can lecture anyone into blinking green.      Now that's gone quite poetic again.      Well, with a curriculum like mine, you’d be well into the blinking green. Though I have no idea what it is you mentioned before, Granddad.      You know, just one of those grandparent phrases that only make sense to us.      Grumpy Englishman lingo? Classic. I’d be lost in the mist.      Oh come on, he's just reminding you both of the olden days, when posters on the walls were only art and not screenshots from bloomin’ TikTok.      That’s true enough. I was reading one in the paper hours ago, talking about all this social media stuff. I couldn’t get over half of the words they used! It's a modern muddle.      My students love to use them, of course. They're trendy but confusing.      So what are we to do, let them scribble nonsense while we eat?      We could review the night's menu.

So do you really think you're gonna drop out, then? I mean, it's not like it's... got to be the end of the world, is it?      I dunno, Lucy. I feel like I've already failed half the exams this term. And it’s not just the work—it’s the stress. It’s like I haven't been myself for months.      I get that. I mean, I never thought I'd be here, to be honest. I was just... happy doing retail full-time when I left school, but Petra kept pushing me to apply. Said I needed to make something of myself.      That’s her, yeah. But what if I fall back into that? You left school and you just... knew what you wanted to do. But I used to be the kid who fell asleep in class, breaking the shoes at the weekend.      Fair. I was the kid running across the sand at Falmouth every morning, didn’t I have soles on my shoes half the time— Mum would go nuts, but I loved it. Used to sneak out in the morning before she woke up.      Oh no, I can imagine! You'd get in such trouble. I was the one who was always getting into scrapes, like, literally. Used to throw rocks at puddles in the car park just for something to do. My mam said I was born with dirt under my nails.      Honestly, I think my name's the only clean thing about me. Lucy? Sounds all posh and proper, but I swear I was a total mess as a kid. Still am most days about it.      Yeah, but you're chaotic in a good way. You've got this energy that keeps you going. I don't feel like I've got that anymore, you know? Like I wake up every day and I just feel like I’m trying to become someone else.      I dunno, maybe that’s what uni’s supposed to do, in a way. But if you've tried and it ain't working out, then do you think you'd regret it if you walked away now?      I go back and forth. Part of me says I’m weak. But another part just says, “You're alive. You’re blooming tired, what can we do about it?”      Oh, I love that. And you know what?

Victoria! Oh my god, it’s so good to see you. I was starting to think you’d forgotten I existed after all these months!      Joanna! I know, I know! It is  so  good to finally have this catch-up! I’ve had the biggest workload at Pearson and then the holidays, and then the start of the new year... it just all escalated. Honestly, I’ve been living in meetings.      Ugh, I totally get it. Project coordination is a bit of a beast too. But this is Oxford, right? Let’s ignore the world for a couple of hours.      Deal. What’s your drink order? I’ll grab them.      Just a gin and tonic, please. I’m driving back after, so maybe I’ll stick to one. You?      Double espresso martini. Strong enough to wake up this town.         Right, now spill the beans. How have you been? Work or otherwise?      Oh, I’ve been up and down! Work has been alright—especially since we’re moving on to a new housing project in Bristol. I’m actually considering a little sabbatical after that one – just to breathe, maybe travel, and actually take time for myself.      That sounds amazing. You always work so hard. And relationships? Still single?      Yes, still single. Let me not even start. It just feels like dating at the minute is like looking at a spreadsheet of toxic traits and being like, “Yup, that’s the one.” Not feeling about it.      Same! I’m currently on “the rebound from no one.” No drama, no love. I’ve actually been focusing a lot on my stepdad. He had a little heart scare, and well, that’s kicked my priorities up a notch.      Oh no! Is he better?      Yeah, thank god, he’s on the mend. But it’s been weird, right? At 25, I suddenly feel like an adult  with  responsibilities. It’s kind of terrifying.      Honestly, that sounds kind of real. I had my mum in for surgery last month. I think we all suddenly get it—how short life is. It’s made me seriously question what I want next in my life.      True. Do you ever see yourself settling down somewhere? Still working in project management long term?      Maybe, but I do love the idea of moving to somewhere like Devon or Cornwall. A slower pace. Less emails and more beaches.      Yeah, I get that.

Right then, Aaron, what’ve ye found on eBay this time then?      Oh... nothing much. Just looking for something cool for my computer. I need a better mouse. The one I got at school is all dodgy, and it keeps clicking on stuff.      Right, well, I don’t want you wastin’ money on no fancy bits o’ gear. A mouse is a mouse. If you’re too quick wi’ it, it’ll go wrong, innit?      But this one’s called a gaming mouse. It has all sorts... like, RGB lights and these buttons—see?—that you can programme to do somethin’. And it’s not even expensive. Less than ten quid.      Ten quid sounds cheap, but these things in the world o’ computers an’ all aren’t always what they seem. When I was teachin’, half the students bought stuff online thinking it was cheap, and then when it arived, it didn’t do what they thought. Or it was broken. I once had a lass come in with a tablet I’d never heard o’. It didn’t even have real apps.      But how would they even sell that? That’s stupid.      Oh, people still do it, lad. There’s lots o’ people out there that don’t know their eBay from their Amazon, and then they get ripped off. Now, what someone says in an advert and what they actually send... aye, there’s a tale.      So, what should I be lookin’ out for then?      Always check the seller’s rating. Don’t just go for the cheapest one. I’ve seen sellers wi’ zero stars because they deliver late or send the wrong thing. And read the description properly. If they say 'like new’ it might mean passed its sell-by date and been used by a thousand people.      I dunno... people in my class just stick the item in and wait. They say it’s quick.      Aye, but if it arives in three weeks and it’s a scrap machine, it’s no good to go, is it? If you want it quick, go with Amazon—still got Prime? It’s faster. But the box might b’full o’ dodgy Chinese batteries instead o’ the item you wanted.      So, maybe I should go with a more trustworthy seller.      That’s the ticket. I tell the students all the time: Always check for reviews. Read the negatives. That's the real truth.

Rather annoying this new council tax bill, isn't it? They've gone and upped it by another ten percent without so much as a by-your-leave. Blows it all out the water, if you ask me.      That is kind of rough, Gramps. I mean, it’s not like we’re rolling in it either, but at least we’ve got a bit more of a say in how our money is spent now. What do you think they’re going to use the extra for, anyway?      I don’t rightly know. Probably end up with blokes walking around with chips on their shoulders filling potholes that were there before the last government, only to do it half-arsed. It’s all madness, I swear. When I were young, you paid your taxes, and things worked, more or less.      Yeah, I guess the old days had their charms, but I’m not sure about all that “good old days” narrative, you know? There was no central heating back then. Also, the potholes were still there.      Oh, I’m not knocking your generation, love. Just saying it feels like we’re paying more for less these days. Still, I suppose it’s something we all just have to grin and bear – unless we all got the same idea and refused to pay altogether, of course.      Maybe, but I highly doubt that’s going to happen. There are people out there who still rely on the system to keep the lights on and the bins collected. I can see you chucking your bill in the fire, but being an actual revolutionary – no thanks.      Fair enough. I’m not a saint, just a grumpy old man who had to work a proper 40-hour week for 40 years and now it feels like the world’s gone mad.      Well, I happen to know a few people who have been on the receiving end of cuts too, so it does feel personal. I mean, I sort out supply chains for a living and I know full well what kind of calculations firms do to keep profits high while balancing the human cost – let’s just say it’s not a nice feeling.      There's a truth in that, love. If it was just me, I'd chuck the whole system into a skip along with blokes who call themselves your employer and make you run the gauntlet for 30 quid an hour.

So do you lot actually know what you're doing for Christmas yet or are you just winging it like me?      We’re going to my aunt’s in Essex. Her house is a mad hodgepodge of vintage stuff, like a fairy-tale gone wrong. We make mince pies all day on Christmas Eve and then just collapse on the sofa on the 25th. What about you?      We’re hosting again, like we do every year. It’s supposed to be cozy, but it always ends up chaotic. We’ve already bought the Christmas pudding and meat, but we need more people who can bring wine. Shout someone to bring supply, Rob.      Yeah, I’ve already got my left arm primed and ready to do the wine shopping if needed, but no pressure. Do you have a strict Christmas Day menu or do you just riff it?      Well, no one can be trusted with the turkey, so I take that on, and Heather always does the veggies. One time, Rob here—      Oh, I’m not even Rob! You don’t need to do that. I only live two streets over.      Mate, it’s Christmas. You’re in. You can bring something sweet, right? Or maybe just act natural while trying not to trip over your own feet after three mince pies.      Fine! I’ll bring something. Maybe a pavlova. Sounds Australian enough. That way, at least one global cuisine will be represented—      Or roadkill.       laughs  Oh, come on, about the roadkill? I thought you bakers had the highest standards.      No! I was just telling you about the time we drove out to the country to do a weekend delivery for the baked goods fair, and we passed this fox on the side of the road. Tail still fluffed up, like it was disappointed in something.      That’s such a  British  thing to say—“disappointed in something.” It was clearly indifferent.      Still, I’m not trying to snack on the side of the road. Unless it’s a nice steak or something.      Which, by the way, we were talking earlier—should we fly one of our family to Australia for Christmas?      Are you mad? On Christmas Day? You can’t just fly on Christmas. That’s like walking into the food court at midnight and expecting a turkey leg. The planes are full, the airports are full of weird people, and the alcohol ratio is definitely off.

Right, so we've got about 40 minutes before we need to meet up in Cambridge. You sorted with the car seats, or shall I bring mine as well?      Sorted! Got two in the back already. No worries. You mind if I take the scenic route via Milton? I saw a place there that does the best flat whites.      Flat whites? You're ambitious. I’m halfway through the drive and I’m already dreaming about a coffee. Just don’t make us late—last time was like a slap in the face when we hit the M11 traffic hell.      Oh come on, it wasn’t  that  bad. I managed to get My Chemical Romance playing full volume with no earphones so we could rally ourselves spiritually. It was emotional, almost life-changing.      Blimey, Nick, you’re a tactical breakfast-time DJ. You need to drop it with a mixtape. “Milton Mornings: 45 Songs to Shatter Your Silence.”      I mean, it  was  brutal waking up to Robin Williams impacts in the back seat yelling “I HATE THIS THING, I HATE GODDO… I HATE IT!” at 8 a.m.      Don't knock it, Dean. It's  experiential . You're not just moving from A to B—you're  feeling  the road.      someone who sounds like they should be narrating a nature documentary. “Now we are on the M11, and it is a stretch of road that will test your patience, but your curiosity will save you.”      I don’t know man, the real question is—how much of what you say online is because of your Brummie accent and how much is just genuine? I swear, I can put someone on FaceTime with my gran and they’ll speak  normally  to a stranger but go on a voice note and suddenly they sound like Queen Elizabeth waiting for a spoon to crack.      Is that regional? I've noticed it too. Like, I do this weird "Cambridge voice" sometimes when I'm trying to sound posh— intentionally . I think it's like a social performance or something.      Oh yeah. I go from bloke on the trains in South London going “move it, innit” to conference seminar roles in Cambridge where I say, “I’m wondering if we might consider the implications…” It’s like walking into a different identity every morning.      I’ve done that when I’ve had to present at work. You see the boardroom, and suddenly you’re Mr. Control-tight-pants-and-boring-words.

So did you lot see the new Billie Eilish track that came out yesterday? It’s so deep... like, I don’t even know how she makes her music sound like that.      Yeah, I streamed it straight away, but I think it's a bit slow for me. Got on to the new  Stranger Things  episode though. Wild stuff! You know how they explained the whole Upside Down theory using quantum mechanics? That was actual physics, right?      Honestly, it’s just fantasy to me, but I get the vibe they want to make it scientific. Though... like, I had Mr. Parson explain quantum entanglement the other day, and it made me want to set fire to my notes. I swear my left hand is allergic to taking down diagrams.      Qualms about physics or the teacher? Or just general existential dread?      Hmm—good question. I mean, Mr. Parson does kind of resemble the science teachers in those 90s cartoons. You know the type—the ones who wear lab coats over jeans and shout at chalkboards like they're in a TED Talk. Like, one time he flicked a beaker with a book and called it a mini experiment.      That was so iconic—he actually missed the beaker and hit the fan. It was  hilarious . I reckon he tries way too hard to be cool. Still, I got an A on our last homework—well, at least I did until my dog decided to audition my books for chew toys.      Ugh, don’t remind me. My dog chewed my USB stick where I had all my music mixes. I about cried. I finally saved the files using the cloud, but it was annoying. I lost like 10% of that track I was working on for Soundtrack Society next term.      You should’ve backed it up earlier. I did that once and had to start a whole new playlist. But hey, it gave me an excuse to listen to more 80s synthwave— Cyberpunk 2077  soundtrack is a new obsession of mine.      You mean  that  one with the synth beats and the weird robotic goth vibes? I tried to get into it, but I personally find it hard not to compare that to  Drive  with Ryan Gosling.      Fair point. I mean,  Drive  sounds like it was made for a neon-lit car chase across a desert of forgotten dreams or something.      That’s like 100% what I visualise when they play the  Cyberpunk  track.

Right, so today was Balanceability day at school, and I think the kids did really well. The first few sessions, they were a bit wobbly, but I can tell their confidence is building.      What's Balanceability, Mummy?      It's a new programme they use at school to help with balance, coordination, and fitness. It's all about body awareness. They do things like walking on beams, doing yoga poses, and jumping jacks. It's quite fun, actually. We've been doing it for a month now.      I fell over... like three times! But mostly because Maisie made me laugh when the teacher told us to do "spider walks." It was too silly!      That doesn't count, Freddie – I didn't fall at all and I did the whole beam!      Well, no doubt about that, Maisie! You were in your element. I even saw your teacher, Mrs. Haydon, say so. You've improved so much, though both of you.      But why do I have to keep doing it? We already did it last week, and the week before...      Because it’s about getting better, Maisie! My Mate Joel told me he can do a handstand now. His mummy said his teacher nearly had a heart attack when he did it in the hall!      Freddie, don’t exaggerate. Anyway, Maisie, you don’t have to rush – it’s not a race. Balance is all about patience. Think of it like being calm as a cat!      NationalCat Day was yesterday! I told us all about it at school. In Japan, they dress cats in little hats and coats and give them toys. I wish our cat, George, had his own celebration.      George wouldn’t like that. He kicked my head when I tried to put a hat on him yesterday. He’s very intense.      He’s not. You just scared him. Anyway, Miss Websites mentioned that some of us might need more help with balancing. She said the next class might be extra special.      Oh, I hope not. But I think Balanceability is helping everyone get more confident in PE. It’s also making Freddie less likely to go splashing face-first into the pool after lunch like he did last term.      That wasn’t my fault! I thought the pool was shallow!      It was, but when you cannonball into it from a diving board? The lifeguard said you left quite the splash. Remember, Freddie, it's not just about jumping – it's about knowing when and how!

Rather annoying isn’t it? I swear I put the kettle on five minutes ago.      What, the kettle or your brain?      Oi! That’s a bit harsh, innit? I’ve been running on about three hours’ sleep all week trying to get on top of that bloody conference we’re setting up in Leeds.      Yeah, I remember that. Hundreds of people, right? Delegates, workshops, breakout sessions. It all sounds exhausting.      It bloody is. Didn’t even get to the gym this week. I was three seconds away from just wearing my tracksuit to work again and calling it a sport.      You should have done! The gym left me last week when I was on the treadmill and Oliver from accounts kept coming up every five minutes to check if I’d seen his emails.      He doesn’t know the meaning of “leave me be.” When’s he ever looked at a computer, anyway?      That’s the blooming thing! Doesn’t he know we have folders? Files? I mean, seriously, it’s like he thinks emails only live on my screen.      Sounds like something outta of  The Office .      I’m not even exaggerating.      Right, don’t get me started on my new boyfriend either. Last night he tells me we should go for a run.      And you said…?       I  said, “What, in the freezing and being poured on by rain?”  He  said, “Exactly!” I mean, what is he trying to do, revive the Spartan mentality?      At least he’s passionate. My last boyfriend only exercised if unloading the dishwasher counted.      There’s a man after my own heart. A bloke with a mentality of “only if I’m getting paid to do it.”      We should form our own group. “The Lazy Lads’ Garden Club.” No exercise, no rain, just tea and biscuits.      I’d sign up for that in a heartbeat. Though I do miss the old gym days though.      I’ll bet. You used to go three times a week when you were training for that half marathon.      Yeah, well, that was back when I had a life without emails and unsavory boyfriends who think walking up a hill counts as a romantic evening.      Okay, true. But still, you both seemed romantic. You once told me you cried when he made you toast the morning after moving in together.      Don’t remind me. I think I might have cried because it was the first time someone didn’t call me at 7 a.m. to confirm if I’d seen their email.

Right then, John, take a seat lad. That pizza’s still steaming. Don’t let it get cold, and I’ll put another log on the fire before it slides out again like last time!      Aw thanks, Auntie Susan! Me? I dunno. Maybe a new pair of trainers? The ones I’ve got now are all holey at the heels.      Aye, them boots are definitely on the last legs! Look at him, getting all cheeky again! I tell ya what—after Easter, lad, I’ll be taking a couple of extra jobs. Might even get the van goin’ on a couple of weekend runs.
